source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּימֵי֙ שְׁפֹ֣ט הַשֹּׁפְטִ֔ים וַיְהִ֥י רָעָ֖ב בָּאָ֑רֶץ וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ אִ֜ישׁ מִבֵּ֧ית לֶ֣חֶם יְהוּדָ֗ה לָגוּר֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב ה֥וּא וְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ וּשְׁנֵ֥י בָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] days of [the] judging of the judges, and there was a famine in the land; and went a man from Bethlehem [of] Judah to sojourn in [the] fields of Moab, he and his wife and [the] two of his sons.

en.L: And it came about in the days when the judges judged that there was a famine in the land. And a man from Bethlehem in Judah went to sojourn in the fields of Moab, he and his wife and his two sons.
en.B: In the days when the judges judged, a famine struck the land. So a man from Bethlehem in Judah set out with his wife and his two sons to live for a while as an outsider in the country of Moab.
en.R: Long ago, in the time when judges led Israel, there was not enough food in the land. A man from the town of Bethlehem in Judah left to live for a time in the country of Moab. He took his wife and his two sons with him.

sw.L: Ikawa katika siku za kuamua kwa waamuzi, palikuwa na njaa katika nchi. Naye mtu mmoja wa Bethlehemu ya Yuda akaenda kukaa kama mgeni katika mashamba ya Moabu, yeye na mkewe na wanawe wawili.
sw.B: Katika siku ambazo waamuzi walikuwa wakiamua, njaa iliipata nchi. Basi mtu mmoja wa Bethlehemu ya Yuda aliondoka pamoja na mkewe na wanawe wawili kwenda kuishi kwa muda kama mgeni katika nchi ya Moabu.
sw.R: Zamani, wakati waamuzi walipowaongoza Israeli, hapakuwa na chakula cha kutosha katika nchi. Mtu mmoja kutoka mji wa Bethlehemu katika Yuda aliondoka kwenda kuishi kwa muda katika nchi ya Moabu. Alimchukua mkewe na wanawe wawili pamoja naye.

es.L: Y sucedió en los días en que juzgaban los jueces, que hubo hambre en la tierra. Y un hombre de Belén de Judá fue a residir como forastero en los campos de Moab, él y su mujer y sus dos hijos.
es.B: En los días en que juzgaban los jueces, hubo hambre en el país. Entonces un hombre de Belén de Judá se fue con su mujer y sus dos hijos a vivir por un tiempo como forastero en la región de Moab.
es.R: Hace mucho tiempo, cuando los jueces dirigían a Israel, no había suficiente comida en el país. Un hombre del pueblo de Belén, en Judá, se fue a vivir por un tiempo en la región de Moab. Se llevó a su esposa y a sus dos hijos.

fr.L: Et il arriva, aux jours où les juges jugeaient, qu’il y eut une famine dans le pays. Et un homme de Bethléem de Juda s’en alla séjourner dans les champs de Moab, lui et sa femme et ses deux fils.
fr.B: Au temps où les juges jugeaient, une famine frappa le pays. Un homme de Bethléem de Juda partit alors avec sa femme et ses deux fils pour vivre quelque temps en immigré dans le pays de Moab.
fr.R: Il y a très longtemps, à l’époque où des juges dirigeaient Israël, il n’y avait plus assez de nourriture dans le pays. Un homme de la ville de Bethléem, en Juda, est parti vivre quelque temps dans le pays de Moab. Il a emmené avec lui sa femme et ses deux fils.

vi.L: Vào thời các quan xét xét xử, trong xứ có nạn đói. Có một người ở Bết-lê-hem thuộc Giu-đa đi kiều ngụ trong đồng ruộng Mô-áp, ông cùng vợ và hai con trai.
vi.B: Vào thời các quan xét xét xử, trong xứ có nạn đói. Vậy một người ở Bết-lê-hem thuộc Giu-đa đem vợ và hai con trai đi đến xứ Mô-áp để sống ở đó một thời gian như khách kiều ngụ.
vi.R: Ngày xưa, vào thời các thủ lĩnh lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên, trong xứ không có đủ lương thực. Một người ở thành Bết-lê-hem thuộc Giu-đa bỏ quê đi đến xứ Mô-áp để sống ở đó một thời gian. Ông đem theo vợ và hai con trai.

ko.L: 사사들이 다스리던 시대에 그 땅에 기근이 들었다. 유다 베들레헴의 한 사람이 모압 들판에 나그네로 살려고 갔는데, 그와 그의 아내와 그의 두 아들이었다.
ko.B: 사사들이 다스리던 시대에 그 땅에 기근이 들었다. 그래서 유다 베들레헴의 한 사람이 아내와 두 아들을 데리고 모압 땅에 가서 얼마 동안 나그네로 살려고 길을 떠났다.
ko.R: 오래전, 사사들이 이스라엘을 이끌던 때에 그 땅에 먹을 것이 모자랐다. 그래서 유다 베들레헴 성의 한 사람이 얼마 동안 모압 땅에 가서 살려고 길을 떠났다. 그는 아내와 두 아들을 데리고 갔다.

pt.L: E aconteceu, nos dias em que os juízes julgavam, que houve fome na terra. E um homem de Belém de Judá foi morar como imigrante nos campos de Moabe, ele, a sua mulher e os seus dois filhos.
pt.B: Nos dias em que os juízes julgavam, houve fome na terra. Então um homem de Belém de Judá partiu com a mulher e os dois filhos para viver por algum tempo como imigrante na terra de Moabe.
pt.R: Muito tempo atrás, na época em que juízes governavam Israel, faltou comida na terra. Um homem da cidade de Belém, em Judá, saiu de lá para morar por um tempo no país de Moabe. Ele levou a mulher e os dois filhos.

decisions.choice: in the days when the judges judged: the time between Joshua and the first kings
decisions.reason: The story is set in the age the book of Judges describes, after Israel entered the land and before it had a king (Judges 2:16-19; 21:25). The judges were leaders the LORD raised up to rescue Israel and govern it (see Judges 2:16). It was a time of unrest and of turning away from the LORD; against it this book tells of quiet loyalty in one family, which ends with the birth of David's grandfather (4:17-22).

decisions.choice: a famine in Bethlehem: hunger in the town whose name means house of bread
decisions.reason: The name Bethlehem means "house of bread" (or food). The story begins with no bread there, and turns when the LORD gives his people bread again (verse 6). The name is not explained in the text, but the contrast runs through the chapter: a full family leaves, and an empty widow comes back at harvest time (verses 21-22).

decisions.choice: to sojourn: to live as a resident outsider
decisions.reason: The verb is used of living for a time in a land not one's own, without the rights of a native, as Abraham did in Egypt during a famine (Genesis 12:10) and Jacob's sons did (Genesis 47:4). The family means to stay only until the famine ends.

decisions.choice: the fields of Moab: the open country of Moab
decisions.reason: The word for "field" here means the open land or territory of a people (Genesis 32:4; Numbers 21:20). Moab lay east of the Dead Sea, a few days' walk from Bethlehem.

decisions.choice: the judges judged (Literal, Balanced); judges led Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Judges, Readable says "led" so a new reader does not picture judges in a court; it adds "Israel", which the phrase means.

decisions.choice: live for a while as an outsider; the country of Moab
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the project's wording for a resident outsider; "country" says what "fields" means here. Literal keeps "sojourn" and "fields".

decisions.choice: "waamuzi" who "walikuwa wakiamua" (judged) at Literal and Balanced; "waamuzi walipowaongoza Israeli" (led Israel) at Readable; "kukaa kama mgeni" for sojourning
decisions.reason: As agreed for Judges in every language, so that Ruth opens in the same words as the book before it: "mwamuzi" and "kuamua" at Literal and Balanced, "kuongoza" at Readable. "Kukaa kama mgeni" says that the family lived in Moab as outsiders without land (m3).

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR" by default, "Yahvé" with the divine name setting; "ustedes" forms by default and "vosotros" / "vosotras" forms with the plural-you setting; "los jueces juzgaban" (L, B), "los jueces dirigían a Israel" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Ruth, as in Judges and the Pentateuch: the divine name is "el SEÑOR" ("del SEÑOR", "al SEÑOR") with "Yahvé" as the setting, and wherever several people are addressed the "ustedes" form is the default with the "vosotros" form of Spain as the setting; when Naomi speaks to her two daughters-in-law the alternative is the feminine "vosotras". The judges' rule is "juzgar" at Literal and Balanced and "dirigir" at Readable, as in Judges.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("il y eut", "partit"); passé composé at Readable ("est parti"); speech in the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Ruth, as the French style guide and the Pentateuch terms list set for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level.

decisions.choice: "les juges jugeaient" (L, B); "des juges dirigeaient Israël" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Ruth, as in Judges: the judges keep their title at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "judges led Israel".

decisions.choice: "các quan xét xét xử" (L, B), "các thủ lĩnh lãnh đạo Y-sơ-ra-ên" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note sets for *shofet* and *shafat*; the same words as the Vietnamese Judges (thủ lĩnh at Readable), so the reader knows which time is meant.

decisions.choice: "사사들이 다스리던 시대" at Literal and Balanced; "사사들이 이스라엘을 이끌던 때" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for the judges in Judges, so that Ruth opens in the same time and words as the book before it.

decisions.choice: Belém de Judá (L, B); a cidade de Belém, em Judá (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "Belém de Judá" is the usual Portuguese form of the town's full name, and "Moabe" the form set in the Pentateuch. Readable says "a cidade de Belém, em Judá", as the English Readable says "the town of". The name's sense, "house of bread" (m2), is left to the meaning note, as in the English.

decisions.choice: morar como imigrante (L); viver por algum tempo como imigrante (B); morar por um tempo (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the verb of the resident outsider (m3) takes "imigrante", the word the Pentateuch sets for the ger, so that Elimelech's family in Moab and Ruth in Israel are seen in the same position. "Estrangeira" is kept for nokhriyyah, the different word Ruth uses of herself in 2:10.

source.text: וְשֵׁ֣ם הָאִ֣ישׁ אֱֽלִימֶ֡לֶךְ וְשֵׁם֩ אִשְׁתּ֨וֹ נָעֳמִ֜י וְשֵׁ֥ם שְׁנֵֽי־בָנָ֣יו׀מַחְל֤וֹן וְכִלְיוֹן֙ אֶפְרָתִ֔ים מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֖חֶם יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ שְׂדֵי־מוֹאָ֖ב וַיִּֽהְיוּ־שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] name of the man [was] Elimelech, and [the] name of his wife Naomi, and [the] name of [the] two of his sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem [of] Judah; and they came [to the] fields of Moab and were there.

en.L: And the name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. And they came to the fields of Moab and remained there.
en.B: The man was called Elimelech, his wife was called Naomi, and his two sons were called Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came into the country of Moab and settled there.
en.R: The man's name was Elimelech, and his wife's name was Naomi. Their two sons were named Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites, from Bethlehem in Judah. They arrived in Moab and stayed there.

sw.L: Na jina la mtu huyo [lilikuwa] Elimeleki, na jina la mkewe Naomi, na majina ya wanawe wawili Maloni na Kilioni, Waefrathi wa Bethlehemu ya Yuda. Nao wakafika katika mashamba ya Moabu, wakakaa huko.
sw.B: Mtu huyo aliitwa Elimeleki, mkewe aliitwa Naomi, na wanawe wawili waliitwa Maloni na Kilioni. Walikuwa Waefrathi wa Bethlehemu ya Yuda. Walifika katika nchi ya Moabu, wakaishi huko.
sw.R: Jina la mtu huyo lilikuwa Elimeleki, na jina la mkewe lilikuwa Naomi. Wana wao wawili waliitwa Maloni na Kilioni. Walikuwa Waefrathi, kutoka Bethlehemu katika Yuda. Walifika Moabu, wakakaa huko.

es.L: Y el nombre del hombre [era] Elimelec, y el nombre de su mujer, Noemí, y los nombres de sus dos hijos, Mahlón y Quelión, efrateos de Belén de Judá. Y llegaron a los campos de Moab y se quedaron allí.
es.B: El hombre se llamaba Elimelec, su mujer se llamaba Noemí y sus dos hijos se llamaban Mahlón y Quelión. Eran efrateos, de Belén de Judá. Llegaron a la región de Moab y se establecieron allí.
es.R: El hombre se llamaba Elimelec, y su esposa se llamaba Noemí. Sus dos hijos se llamaban Mahlón y Quelión. Eran efrateos, de Belén de Judá. Llegaron a Moab y se quedaron allí.

fr.L: Et le nom de l’homme [était] Élimélek, et le nom de sa femme Noémi, et le nom de ses deux fils Mahlôn et Kilyôn, des Éphratiens de Bethléem de Juda. Et ils arrivèrent dans les champs de Moab et y restèrent.
fr.B: L’homme s’appelait Élimélek, sa femme Noémi, et ses deux fils Mahlôn et Kilyôn. C’étaient des Éphratiens, de Bethléem de Juda. Ils arrivèrent dans le pays de Moab et s’y établirent.
fr.R: L’homme s’appelait Élimélek, et sa femme s’appelait Noémi. Leurs deux fils s’appelaient Mahlôn et Kilyôn. C’étaient des Éphratiens, de Bethléem de Juda. Ils sont arrivés en Moab et ils y sont restés.

vi.L: Người ấy tên là Ê-li-mê-léc, vợ tên là Na-ô-mi, và hai con trai tên là Mạc-lôn và Ki-li-ôn, là người Ép-ra-ta ở Bết-lê-hem thuộc Giu-đa. Họ đến đồng ruộng Mô-áp và ở lại đó.
vi.B: Người ấy tên là Ê-li-mê-léc, vợ ông tên là Na-ô-mi, và hai con trai tên là Mạc-lôn và Ki-li-ôn. Họ là người Ép-ra-ta ở Bết-lê-hem thuộc Giu-đa. Họ đến xứ Mô-áp và định cư ở đó.
vi.R: Người ấy tên là Ê-li-mê-léc, còn vợ ông tên là Na-ô-mi. Hai con trai của họ tên là Mạc-lôn và Ki-li-ôn. Họ là người Ép-ra-ta, ở Bết-lê-hem thuộc Giu-đa. Họ đến Mô-áp và ở lại đó.

ko.L: 그 사람의 이름은 엘리멜렉이고, 그의 아내의 이름은 나오미이고, 그의 두 아들의 이름은 말론과 기룐이었다. 그들은 유다 베들레헴 출신의 에브랏 사람들이었다. 그들은 모압 들판에 가서 거기에서 살았다.
ko.B: 그 사람의 이름은 엘리멜렉이고, 그의 아내는 나오미, 두 아들은 말론과 기룐이었다. 그들은 유다 베들레헴 출신의 에브랏 사람들이었다. 그들은 모압 땅에 가서 거기에 자리 잡고 살았다.
ko.R: 그 사람의 이름은 엘리멜렉이고, 그의 아내의 이름은 나오미였다. 그들의 두 아들은 말론과 기룐이었다. 그들은 유다 베들레헴 출신의 에브랏 사람들이었다. 그들은 모압에 가서 거기에 머물러 살았다.

pt.L: E o nome do homem [era] Elimeleque, e o nome da sua mulher, Noemi, e o nome dos seus dois filhos, Malom e Quiliom, efrateus de Belém de Judá. E eles chegaram aos campos de Moabe e ficaram ali.
pt.B: O homem se chamava Elimeleque, a mulher se chamava Noemi, e os dois filhos se chamavam Malom e Quiliom. Eram efrateus, de Belém de Judá. Eles chegaram à terra de Moabe e se estabeleceram ali.
pt.R: O nome do homem era Elimeleque, e o nome da mulher dele era Noemi. Os dois filhos se chamavam Malom e Quiliom. Eles eram efrateus, de Belém, em Judá. Eles chegaram a Moabe e ficaram morando lá.

decisions.choice: Ephrathites: people of Ephrath, the district of Bethlehem
decisions.reason: Ephrath is an old name for Bethlehem or the area around it (Genesis 35:19; 48:7; Micah 5:1). David's father Jesse is called "an Ephrathite from Bethlehem in Judah" in the same words (1 Samuel 17:12), so the name already points toward the end of the book (4:11, 17).

decisions.choice: the names: Elimelech "my God is king", Naomi "pleasant"; Mahlon and Chilion perhaps "sickness" and "failing"
decisions.reason: Elimelech means "my God is king", a striking name in a time with no king (Judges 21:25). Naomi means "pleasant" or "my pleasantness", and she plays on it in verse 20. Mahlon and Chilion sound like words for being sick and for coming to an end, which fits their early deaths, but the meaning of these two names is not certain and the text does not comment on them.

decisions.choice: settled there; stayed there
decisions.reason: "Were there" means they lived there; Balanced and Readable say so. Literal has "remained there".

decisions.choice: "Elimeleki", "Naomi", "Maloni", "Kilioni", "Waefrathi"; later "Orpa", "Ruthu", "Boazi", "Obedi"
decisions.reason: The names of Ruth as agreed for every language: Ruthu, Boazi and Obedi as already printed in Matthew 1:5; the others follow the Hebrew with the final vowel Swahili writes.

decisions.choice: "Elimelec", "Noemí", "Mahlón", "Quelión", "Orfa", "Rut", "Booz", "Obed"
decisions.reason: The names in their usual Spanish forms, as the terms note sets; "Rut", "Booz" and "Obed" are the forms Spanish already uses in Matthew 1:5, and the genealogy of chapter 4 follows Matthew 1:3-6 (Fares, Hezrón, Ram, Aminadab, Naasón, Salmón, Isaí).

decisions.choice: "Élimélek", "Noémi", "Mahlôn", "Kilyôn", "Orpa", "Ruth", "Booz", "Obed"; "les Éphratiens"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Ruth, as the terms note for these books sets: Naomi, Ruth, Orpah, Boaz, Elimelech and Obed take their usual French forms, and Boaz, Obed and Ruth are already written so in Matthew 1:5 in this translation. Mahlon and Chilion, with no established French form, are transcribed from the Hebrew as the French of the Pentateuch does.

decisions.choice: "Ê-li-mê-léc", "Na-ô-mi", "Mạc-lôn", "Ki-li-ôn", "người Ép-ra-ta"
decisions.reason: Elimelech and Naomi as the Joshua–Ruth terms note; the other names in the usual Protestant forms, kept through the book.

decisions.choice: Elimeleque, Noemi, Malom, Quiliom
decisions.reason: For the whole book, the usual Brazilian forms of the names; with Orfa, Rute, Boaz, Obede, Jessé and Davi later in the book (Matthew 1:5 has Boaz, Obede, Rute in Portuguese). Their meanings (m2) are left to the meaning note, except where Naomi plays on her own name (1:20).

decisions.choice: efrateus
decisions.reason: "Efrateus" is the people of Efrata, the form Genesis 35:19 has in Portuguese for the district of Bethlehem (m1); it keeps the link with Jesse, "o efrateu de Belém de Judá" (1 Samuel 17:12). Every level keeps the word, as the English keeps "Ephrathites".

source.text: וַיָּ֥מָת אֱלִימֶ֖לֶךְ אִ֣ישׁ נָעֳמִ֑י וַתִּשָּׁאֵ֥ר הִ֖יא וּשְׁנֵ֥י בָנֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And died Elimelech, [the] husband of Naomi, and she was left, she and her two sons.

en.L: And Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left, she and her two sons.
en.B: Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, leaving her with her two sons.
en.R: Then Naomi's husband Elimelech died. Naomi was left with only her two sons.

sw.L: Naye Elimeleki, mume wa Naomi, akafa, naye akabaki, yeye na wanawe wawili.
sw.B: Kisha Elimeleki, mume wa Naomi, alikufa, akamwacha pamoja na wanawe wawili.
sw.R: Kisha mume wa Naomi, Elimeleki, alikufa. Naomi alibaki na wanawe wawili tu.

es.L: Y murió Elimelec, el marido de Noemí, y quedó ella con sus dos hijos.
es.B: Después murió Elimelec, el marido de Noemí, y ella se quedó con sus dos hijos.
es.R: Después murió Elimelec, el esposo de Noemí. Noemí se quedó sola con sus dos hijos.

fr.L: Et Élimélek, le mari de Noémi, mourut, et elle resta, elle et ses deux fils.
fr.B: Puis Élimélek, le mari de Noémi, mourut, et elle resta avec ses deux fils.
fr.R: Ensuite, Élimélek, le mari de Noémi, est mort. Noémi est restée seule avec ses deux fils.

vi.L: Ê-li-mê-léc, chồng của Na-ô-mi, qua đời, và bà còn lại với hai con trai.
vi.B: Rồi Ê-li-mê-léc, chồng của Na-ô-mi, qua đời, để lại bà với hai con trai.
vi.R: Rồi Ê-li-mê-léc, chồng của Na-ô-mi, qua đời. Na-ô-mi chỉ còn lại hai con trai.

ko.L: 나오미의 남편 엘리멜렉이 죽고, 나오미와 그의 두 아들만 남았다.
ko.B: 그런데 나오미의 남편 엘리멜렉이 죽고, 나오미는 두 아들과 함께 남았다.
ko.R: 그런데 나오미의 남편 엘리멜렉이 죽었다. 나오미에게는 두 아들만 남았다.

pt.L: E morreu Elimeleque, marido de Noemi, e ela ficou, ela e os seus dois filhos.
pt.B: Depois Elimeleque, marido de Noemi, morreu, e ela ficou com os dois filhos.
pt.R: Então Elimeleque, o marido de Noemi, morreu. Noemi ficou só com os dois filhos.

decisions.choice: she was left: the first of Naomi's losses
decisions.reason: The same verb returns in verse 5, when she is left without her sons as well. The narrator tells the story from Naomi's side: each death is counted as a loss to her.

decisions.choice: left with only her two sons
decisions.reason: "Only" brings out that her husband was now gone and her sons were all the family she had; the Hebrew implies it by setting "she and her two sons" after the death.

source.text: וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ לָהֶ֗ם נָשִׁים֙ מֹֽאֲבִיּ֔וֹת שֵׁ֤ם הָֽאַחַת֙ עָרְפָּ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית ר֑וּת וַיֵּ֥שְׁבוּ שָׁ֖ם כְּעֶ֥שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took for themselves wives, Moabite [women]; [the] name of the one [was] Orpah, and [the] name of the second Ruth; and they lived there about ten years.

en.L: And they took for themselves Moabite wives; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the second was Ruth. And they lived there about ten years.
en.B: The sons married Moabite women, one named Orpah and the other named Ruth. They lived there for about ten years.
en.R: Both sons married women from Moab. One was named Orpah, and the other was named Ruth. The family lived in Moab for about ten years.

sw.L: Nao wakajitwalia wake, wanawake wa Kimoabu; jina la mmoja [lilikuwa] Orpa, na jina la wa pili Ruthu. Nao wakakaa huko yapata miaka kumi.
sw.B: Wana hao walioa wanawake wa Kimoabu, mmoja aitwaye Orpa na mwingine aitwaye Ruthu. Waliishi huko kwa muda wa miaka kumi hivi.
sw.R: Wana wote wawili walioa wanawake wa Moabu. Mmoja aliitwa Orpa, na mwingine aliitwa Ruthu. Jamaa hiyo iliishi Moabu kwa muda wa miaka kumi hivi.

es.L: Y tomaron para sí mujeres moabitas; el nombre de una [era] Orfa, y el nombre de la otra, Rut. Y habitaron allí unos diez años.
es.B: Los hijos se casaron con mujeres moabitas; una se llamaba Orfa y la otra Rut. Vivieron allí unos diez años.
es.R: Los dos hijos se casaron con mujeres de Moab. Una se llamaba Orfa, y la otra se llamaba Rut. La familia vivió en Moab unos diez años.

fr.L: Et ils prirent pour eux des femmes moabites ; le nom de l’une [était] Orpa, et le nom de la seconde Ruth. Et ils habitèrent là environ dix ans.
fr.B: Les fils épousèrent des Moabites ; l’une s’appelait Orpa et l’autre Ruth. Ils vécurent là une dizaine d’années.
fr.R: Les deux fils ont épousé des femmes de Moab. L’une s’appelait Orpa, et l’autre s’appelait Ruth. La famille a vécu en Moab pendant environ dix ans.

vi.L: Họ cưới cho mình những người vợ Mô-áp; một người tên là Ọt-ba, người kia tên là Ru-tơ. Họ sống ở đó khoảng mười năm.
vi.B: Hai người con trai cưới vợ là người Mô-áp, một người tên là Ọt-ba, còn người kia tên là Ru-tơ. Họ sống ở đó khoảng mười năm.
vi.R: Cả hai người con trai đều cưới vợ là người Mô-áp. Một người tên là Ọt-ba, còn người kia tên là Ru-tơ. Gia đình ấy sống ở Mô-áp khoảng mười năm.

ko.L: 그들은 모압 여자들을 아내로 맞았는데, 한 사람의 이름은 오르바이고 다른 한 사람의 이름은 룻이었다. 그들은 거기에서 십 년쯤 살았다.
ko.B: 두 아들은 모압 여자들과 결혼했는데, 한 사람은 오르바이고 다른 한 사람은 룻이었다. 그들은 거기에서 십 년쯤 살았다.
ko.R: 두 아들은 모두 모압 여자와 결혼했다. 한 사람의 이름은 오르바였고, 다른 한 사람의 이름은 룻이었다. 그 가족은 모압에서 십 년쯤 살았다.

pt.L: E eles tomaram para si mulheres moabitas; o nome de uma [era] Orfa, e o nome da segunda, Rute. E moraram ali uns dez anos.
pt.B: Os filhos se casaram com mulheres moabitas, uma chamada Orfa e a outra chamada Rute. Eles moraram ali cerca de dez anos.
pt.R: Os dois filhos se casaram com mulheres de Moabe. Uma se chamava Orfa, e a outra se chamava Rute. A família morou em Moabe uns dez anos.

decisions.choice: took wives: married
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to lift or carry; with "wives" it means to marry, a way of saying it found mostly in later books (Ezra 10:44; 2 Chronicles 11:21).

decisions.choice: Moabite women: wives from a people outside Israel
decisions.reason: Moab was a neighbor with a troubled history with Israel (Numbers 22-25), and the law kept Moabites out of the LORD's assembly (Deuteronomy 23:4). The narrator does not comment on the marriages; the question of a Moabite woman joining Israel is the heart of the story (1:16; 2:10-12; 4:10).

decisions.choice: about ten years: the length of the stay in Moab
decisions.reason: The ten years are counted after the marriages, but they may cover the family's whole time in Moab. Either way, the marriages had produced no children (4:13 is Ruth's first child).

decisions.choice: The sons (Balanced); Both sons (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they"; Balanced and Readable name who married, so a reader does not think of Naomi.

decisions.choice: "Ọt-ba" and "Ru-tơ"
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note; "Ru-tơ" is the form published in Matthew 1:5.

decisions.choice: mulheres moabitas (L, B); mulheres de Moabe (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the people of Moab are "moabita(s)", and Ruth's title is "Rute, a moabita" (1:22; 2:2, 21; 4:5, 10). Readable says "de Moabe" here, as the English Readable says "from Moab".

source.text: וַיָּמ֥וּתוּ גַם־שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם מַחְל֣וֹן וְכִלְי֑וֹן וַתִּשָּׁאֵר֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה מִשְּׁנֵ֥י יְלָדֶ֖יהָ וּמֵאִישָֽׁהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And died also [the] two of them, Mahlon and Chilion, and was left the woman without her two children and without her husband.

en.L: And both of them also died, Mahlon and Chilion, and the woman was left without her two children and without her husband.
en.B: Then both Mahlon and Chilion died as well, and the woman was left alone, without her two sons and without her husband.
en.R: Then Mahlon and Chilion died too. Naomi had lost both her sons and her husband.

sw.L: Nao wote wawili, Maloni na Kilioni, wakafa pia, naye yule mwanamke akabaki bila watoto wake wawili na bila mumewe.
sw.B: Kisha Maloni na Kilioni nao walikufa wote wawili, na yule mwanamke akabaki peke yake, bila wanawe wawili na bila mumewe.
sw.R: Kisha Maloni na Kilioni nao walikufa. Naomi alikuwa amewapoteza wanawe wote wawili na mumewe.

es.L: Y murieron también los dos, Mahlón y Quelión, y quedó la mujer sin sus dos hijos y sin su marido.
es.B: Después murieron también Mahlón y Quelión, y la mujer se quedó sola, sin sus dos hijos y sin su marido.
es.R: Después murieron también Mahlón y Quelión. Noemí había perdido a sus dos hijos y a su esposo.

fr.L: Et tous deux moururent aussi, Mahlôn et Kilyôn, et la femme resta privée de ses deux enfants et de son mari.
fr.B: Puis Mahlôn et Kilyôn moururent eux aussi, et la femme resta seule, sans ses deux fils et sans son mari.
fr.R: Ensuite, Mahlôn et Kilyôn sont morts eux aussi. Noémi avait perdu ses deux fils et son mari.

vi.L: Cả hai người, Mạc-lôn và Ki-li-ôn, cũng qua đời, và người đàn bà còn lại, không còn hai đứa con và không còn chồng.
vi.B: Rồi cả Mạc-lôn lẫn Ki-li-ôn cũng qua đời, và người đàn bà còn lại một mình, không còn hai con trai, cũng không còn chồng.
vi.R: Rồi Mạc-lôn và Ki-li-ôn cũng qua đời. Na-ô-mi đã mất cả hai con trai lẫn chồng mình.

ko.L: 그런데 말론과 기룐 두 사람도 죽어서, 그 여자는 두 아이와 남편을 잃고 홀로 남았다.
ko.B: 그러다가 말론과 기룐도 둘 다 죽었다. 그 여자는 두 아들도 남편도 없이 홀로 남게 되었다.
ko.R: 그러다가 말론과 기룐도 죽었다. 나오미는 두 아들과 남편을 모두 잃었다.

pt.L: E morreram também os dois, Malom e Quiliom, e a mulher ficou sem os seus dois filhos e sem o seu marido.
pt.B: Depois Malom e Quiliom também morreram, e a mulher ficou sozinha, sem os dois filhos e sem o marido.
pt.R: Então Malom e Quiliom também morreram. Noemi perdeu os dois filhos e o marido.

decisions.choice: her two children: her sons, seen as her children
decisions.reason: The word means a young child or boy, though the sons were grown and married. It looks at them as Naomi's children, the ones she bore. The same word is used for the child Naomi holds at the end of the book (4:16), when what she lost is restored.

decisions.choice: the woman was left: Naomi alone
decisions.reason: She is not named here but called "the woman", which makes her stand alone in the scene. The verb "was left" repeats verse 3: now no man of her family remains.

decisions.choice: sons
decisions.reason: "Children" in English would suggest small children; Balanced and Readable say "sons". Literal keeps "children".

decisions.choice: left alone (Balanced); Naomi (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "alone", which the two "without" phrases mean; Readable names "the woman" so a new reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: os seus dois filhos (every level)
decisions.reason: The English Literal keeps "children" for the word for a young child (m1). Portuguese "filhos" already means one's children at any age, as Naomi sees them; "meninos" or "crianças" would make grown men small boys. So Literal says "filhos" too, and the meaning note keeps the link with the child of 4:16.

source.text: וַתָּ֤קָם הִיא֙ וְכַלֹּתֶ֔יהָ וַתָּ֖שָׁב מִשְּׂדֵ֣י מוֹאָ֑ב כִּ֤י שָֽׁמְעָה֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב כִּֽי־פָקַ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־עַמּ֔וֹ לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם לָֽחֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And she arose, she and her daughters-in-law, and she returned from [the] fields of Moab, for she had heard in [the] field of Moab that YHWH had visited his people to give to them bread.

en.L: And she arose with her daughters-in-law and turned back from the fields of Moab, for she had heard in the field of Moab that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had visited {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people to give them bread.
en.B: Then she got ready with her daughters-in-law to go back from the country of Moab, because she had heard there that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had come to the help of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and given them food.
en.R: While she was still in Moab, Naomi heard that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had cared for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people by giving them food again. So she and her daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go back home.

sw.L: Naye akaondoka pamoja na wakwe zake, akarudi kutoka mashamba ya Moabu, kwa maana alikuwa amesikia katika shamba la Moabu kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewajilia watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ili awape chakula.
sw.B: Kisha alijiandaa pamoja na wakwe zake kurudi kutoka nchi ya Moabu, kwa sababu alikuwa amesikia huko kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewasaidia watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na kuwapa chakula.
sw.R: Naomi alipokuwa bado Moabu, alisikia kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewatunza watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa kuwapa chakula tena. Kwa hiyo yeye na wakwe zake walijiandaa kuondoka Moabu ili warudi nyumbani.

es.L: Y se levantó con sus nueras y volvió de los campos de Moab, porque había oído en el campo de Moab que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había visitado a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo para darles pan.
es.B: Entonces se dispuso a regresar de la región de Moab con sus nueras, porque había oído allí que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había acudido en ayuda de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo y le había dado alimento.
es.R: Estando todavía en Moab, Noemí oyó que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había cuidado de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo dándole otra vez alimento. Así que ella y sus nueras se prepararon para dejar Moab y volver a su tierra.

fr.L: Et elle se leva avec ses belles-filles et s’en retourna des champs de Moab, car elle avait entendu dans le champ de Moab que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait visité {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple pour lui donner du pain.
fr.B: Alors elle se prépara avec ses belles-filles à quitter le pays de Moab, car elle avait appris là-bas que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était venu en aide à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple en lui donnant de quoi manger.
fr.R: Pendant qu’elle était encore en Moab, Noémi a appris que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait pris soin de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple en lui donnant de nouveau de la nourriture. Alors, avec ses belles-filles, elle s’est préparée à quitter Moab pour rentrer chez elle.

vi.L: Bà đứng dậy cùng các con dâu để trở về từ đồng ruộng Mô-áp, vì bà đã nghe tại đồng ruộng Mô-áp rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thăm viếng dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và ban bánh cho họ.
vi.B: Bấy giờ bà cùng các con dâu chuẩn bị rời xứ Mô-áp trở về, vì ở đó bà nghe tin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đến giúp đỡ dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và ban lương thực cho họ.
vi.R: Khi còn ở Mô-áp, Na-ô-mi nghe tin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã chăm sóc dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bằng cách lại ban lương thực cho họ. Vậy bà và các con dâu chuẩn bị rời Mô-áp trở về quê.

ko.L: 나오미는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 백성을 돌아보셔서 그들에게 양식을 주셨다는 말을 모압 들판에서 들었다. 그래서 그는 며느리들과 함께 일어나 모압 들판에서 돌아가려고 하였다.
ko.B: 그때 나오미는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 백성을 찾아와 도우시고 그들에게 양식을 주셨다는 소식을 모압 땅에서 들었다. 그래서 나오미는 며느리들과 함께 모압 땅을 떠나 돌아갈 채비를 하였다.
ko.R: 나오미는 아직 모압에 있을 때, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 백성을 돌보셔서 다시 먹을 것을 주셨다는 소식을 들었다. 그래서 나오미는 며느리들과 함께 모압을 떠나 고향으로 돌아갈 준비를 하였다.

pt.L: E ela se levantou com as suas noras e voltou dos campos de Moabe, porque tinha ouvido no campo de Moabe que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha visitado o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo para lhes dar pão.
pt.B: Então ela se preparou com as noras para voltar da terra de Moabe, pois tinha ouvido ali que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha vindo em socorro do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo e lhe dado alimento.
pt.R: Ainda em Moabe, Noemi ouviu dizer que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha cuidado do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo e lhe dado comida outra vez. Então ela e as noras se prepararam para sair de Moabe e voltar para casa.

decisions.choice: visited his people: came to care for them
decisions.reason: The verb means to give attention to someone, to look after them. When God "visits" his people he steps in to help them (Genesis 21:1; 50:24; Exodus 4:31). Here his help is the end of the famine.

decisions.choice: bread: food, the harvest
decisions.reason: The word means bread and so food in general. It answers the famine of verse 1 and echoes the name Bethlehem, "house of bread".

decisions.choice: returned: began the journey back
decisions.reason: The verb "return" (or "turn back") is the key word of the chapter and appears again and again (verses 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 21, 22). Here it names the start of the journey; verse 22 tells its end.

decisions.choice: food
decisions.reason: In English "bread" would sound like one food only; Balanced and Readable say "food". Literal keeps "bread".

decisions.choice: news first, then the journey; "again"
decisions.reason: Readable tells what Naomi heard before what she did, the order in which things happened. "Again" makes clear that the famine had ended.

decisions.choice: the divine name as "BWANA" in capitals by default, with "Yahwe" as the reader setting, for the whole of Ruth; "wakwe zake" for her daughters-in-law
decisions.reason: As in Judges and the Pentateuch drafts: "BWANA" in capitals shows that the name stands in the Hebrew, as the English "the LORD" does. "Mkwe" is the Swahili word for a child-in-law, used here for the two young women.

decisions.choice: the divine name as "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals, with "Yahvé" as the reader setting; "son" for the LORD under the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: For the whole of Ruth, as in the Pentateuch and Judges: the name is written "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals, like the English "the LORD", and the setting gives "Yahvé"; "l'Éternel" is the alternative a reviewer may prefer. Pronouns for God take the deity pronoun setting wherever the English has one.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span: "그분의 백성" for "his people"
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect for God is carried by "그분" and the honorific at every level.

source.text: וַתֵּצֵ֗א מִן־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיְתָה־שָׁ֔מָּה וּשְׁתֵּ֥י כַלֹּתֶ֖יהָ עִמָּ֑הּ וַתֵּלַ֣כְנָה בַדֶּ֔רֶךְ לָשׁ֖וּב אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And she went out from the place where she had been there, and [the] two of her daughters-in-law with her, and they went on the way to return to [the] land of Judah.

en.L: And she went out from the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they went on the road to return to the land of Judah.
en.B: She set out from the place where she had been living, with her two daughters-in-law, and they took the road back to the land of Judah.
en.R: She left the place where she had been living, and her two daughters-in-law went with her. They started down the road that led back to Judah.

sw.L: Naye akatoka mahali alipokuwa, na wakwe zake wawili pamoja naye, wakaenda njiani kurudi nchi ya Yuda.
sw.B: Aliondoka mahali alipokuwa akiishi pamoja na wakwe zake wawili, wakashika njia ya kurudi nchi ya Yuda.
sw.R: Aliondoka mahali alipokuwa akiishi, na wakwe zake wawili walikwenda pamoja naye. Walianza safari kwenye njia iliyorudi Yuda.

es.L: Y salió del lugar donde había estado, y sus dos nueras con ella, y fueron por el camino para volver a la tierra de Judá.
es.B: Salió del lugar donde había vivido, junto con sus dos nueras, y tomaron el camino de vuelta a la tierra de Judá.
es.R: Dejó el lugar donde había vivido, y sus dos nueras se fueron con ella. Emprendieron el camino que llevaba de vuelta a Judá.

fr.L: Et elle sortit du lieu où elle avait été, et ses deux belles-filles avec elle, et elles s’en allèrent sur le chemin pour retourner au pays de Juda.
fr.B: Elle quitta l’endroit où elle avait vécu, avec ses deux belles-filles, et elles prirent le chemin du retour vers le pays de Juda.
fr.R: Elle a quitté l’endroit où elle avait vécu, et ses deux belles-filles sont parties avec elle. Elles ont pris la route qui ramenait en Juda.

vi.L: Bà rời khỏi nơi mình đã ở, cùng với hai con dâu, và họ lên đường trở về xứ Giu-đa.
vi.B: Bà rời khỏi nơi mình đã sống cùng với hai con dâu, và họ lên đường trở về xứ Giu-đa.

fr.L: Et Noémi dit à ses deux belles-filles : « Allez, retournez, chacune à la maison de sa mère. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} agisse envers vous avec amour loyal, comme vous avez agi envers les morts et envers moi.
fr.B: Mais Noémi dit à ses deux belles-filles : « Rentrez chez vous, toutes les deux, chacune dans la maison de sa mère. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous montre un amour fidèle, comme vous l’avez montré à ceux qui sont morts et à moi.
fr.R: Alors Noémi a dit à ses deux belles-filles : « Retournez chez vous, toutes les deux, chez votre mère. Vous avez montré un amour fidèle à vos maris qui sont morts, et à moi aussi. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous montre le même amour fidèle.

vi.L: Na-ô-mi nói với hai con dâu: "Hãy đi, mỗi con hãy trở về nhà mẹ mình. Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đối xử với các con bằng tình yêu thương thành tín, như các con đã đối xử với những người đã chết và với mẹ.
vi.B: Nhưng Na-ô-mi nói với hai con dâu: "Các con hãy trở về, mỗi con về nhà mẹ mình. Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} tỏ tình yêu thương thành tín với các con, như các con đã tỏ ra với những người đã khuất và với mẹ.
vi.R: Rồi Na-ô-mi nói với hai con dâu: "Cả hai con nên trở về nhà mẹ mình. Các con đã tỏ tình thương thành tín với chồng các con, là những người đã qua đời, và với mẹ. Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cũng tỏ tình thương thành tín như vậy với các con.

ko.L: 그때 나오미가 두 며느리에게 말했다. "가거라, 너희는 저마다 너희 어머니의 집으로 돌아가거라. 너희가 죽은 사람들과 나에게 한결같은 사랑을 베푼 것처럼, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희에게 한결같은 사랑을 베푸시기를 바란다.
ko.B: 그러나 나오미가 두 며느리에게 말했다. "너희는 저마다 친정어머니의 집으로 돌아가거라. 너희가 세상을 떠난 남편들과 나에게 한결같은 사랑을 보여 준 것처럼, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서도 너희에게 한결같은 사랑을 보여 주시기를 바란다.
ko.R: 그때 나오미가 두 며느리에게 말했다. "너희는 둘 다 친정어머니에게 돌아가거라. 너희는 죽은 남편들과 나에게 변함없는 사랑을 보여 주었다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서도 너희에게 그와 같은 변함없는 사랑을 보여 주시기를 바란다.

pt.L: E Noemi disse às suas duas noras: "Vão, voltem, cada uma para a casa da sua mãe. Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} use de amor leal com vocês, como vocês usaram com os mortos e comigo.
pt.B: Mas Noemi disse às duas noras: "Vão para casa, as duas, cada uma para a casa da sua mãe. Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} mostre amor leal a vocês, assim como vocês o mostraram aos que morreram e a mim.
pt.R: Então Noemi disse às duas noras: "Vocês duas devem voltar para casa, para junto das suas mães. Vocês mostraram bondade leal aos seus maridos que morreram e a mim. Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, do mesmo modo, mostre a vocês o seu amor leal.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal goodness that keeps faith with others
decisions.reason: Chesed is goodness shown out of loyalty, more than duty requires, to someone to whom one is bound. It is used of the LORD's covenant love (Exodus 34:6) and of people keeping faith with each other (Joshua 2:12). The young women have kept faith with their husbands and with Naomi; Naomi asks the LORD to keep faith with them in the same way. The word comes back at key points of the book (2:20; 3:10), and the story shows it lived out.

decisions.choice: her mother's house: home, where a new marriage would be arranged
decisions.reason: A widow usually went back to her "father's house" (Genesis 38:11; Leviticus 22:13). "Mother's house" is rarer and is used where marriage is in view (Genesis 24:28; Song of Songs 3:4; 8:2). Naomi is sending them home to marry again, as verse 9 says.

decisions.choice: may he deal: the short form of the verb, marking a wish
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text (ketiv) give the long form of the verb "he will do"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is the short form used for a wish. Either way Naomi is praying for the women; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: you: the women addressed with masculine plural forms
decisions.reason: Several words addressed to the two women have masculine plural endings (here and in verses 9, 11 and 13). Hebrew sometimes uses these forms for a group of women, and the book does so more than once (4:11); it does not change who is meant.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6, Deuteronomy and Joshua 2:12, so that the loyalty in the word is kept; "kindness" alone would leave it out. The same wording is kept at every occurrence in Ruth (2:20; 3:10).

decisions.choice: what they have done first, then the wish; "your husbands"
decisions.reason: Readable tells what the women have done before Naomi's prayer, so the "same faithful love" is clear. "The dead" are first of all the women's husbands (verse 5), so Readable names them.

decisions.choice: "upendo usiokoma" (unfailing love) for chesed, the same words for the LORD's love and for the young women's
decisions.reason: As agreed with Psalms for every language. Naomi uses one word for what the women did and what she asks of the LORD, so Swahili keeps one expression for both; "fadhili", the word for kindness between people, is kept for 3:10, where only people are in view.

decisions.choice: "amor leal" (L); "amor fiel" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for this word in Ruth, as in Psalms: the loyal goodness that keeps faith with others (m1) is "amor leal" at Literal and "amor fiel" at Balanced and Readable, the same words for the LORD's love and for the love the young women have shown, so the reader sees the link Naomi makes.

decisions.choice: "amour loyal" (L); "amour fidèle" (B, R)
alternatives: "bonté", which the terms note keeps for kindness between people
decisions.reason: For the whole of Ruth, as the terms note for these books and the Psalms set for the Hebrew word: the loyal love that keeps faith with others (m1), here asked of the LORD and already shown by the two women, so the same word serves for both. Literal "amour loyal", Balanced and Readable "amour fidèle", as the English "steadfast love" and "faithful love". The word returns in 2:20 and 3:10.

decisions.choice: "vous" to the two women; Naomi says "tu" to one of them, and Ruth says "tu" to Naomi
alternatives: "vous" of respect from Ruth to her mother-in-law
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets: "tu" to one person and "vous" to several, as modern French Bibles do; "vous" for one person would be a different register, not a regional variant.

decisions.choice: "tình yêu thương thành tín" (L, B), "tình thương thành tín" (R) for *hesed*
decisions.reason: As the Psalms and Genesis notes set; one word covers both the LORD's love and the daughters-in-law's loyalty, so that the reader sees it is the same *hesed*.

decisions.choice: Naomi says "mẹ" and "các con"; the daughters-in-law say "mẹ" and "chúng con"
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note sets for Naomi and Ruth: a mother-in-law and her sons' wives speak as mother and daughters.

decisions.choice: "한결같은 사랑" at Literal and Balanced; "변함없는 사랑" at Readable
decisions.reason: *Hesed* is rendered as in Psalms and Genesis, so that the same word is heard when the LORD shows it and when the young widows have shown it; the book turns on this word (2:20; 3:10).

decisions.choice: Naomi speaks to her daughters-in-law in the plain style (해라체) with "내 딸들아"; they answer her in the polite informal style (해요체) with "어머님"
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set: a mother-in-law speaks to her sons' wives as to daughters, and they answer with warmth and respect.

decisions.choice: amor leal (L, B); bondade leal for the women's and amor leal for the LORD's (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: chesed (m1) follows 1 and 2 Samuel and Kings in Portuguese: "amor leal" for the LORD's chesed; "lealdade" at Literal and Balanced and "bondade leal" (or "bondoso e leal") at Readable where it is shown between people (2:20 is read with the LORD; 3:10 is Ruth's). At Literal and Balanced the Hebrew names only the LORD's chesed and refers back to it for what the women did ("como vocês usaram", "o mostraram"), so the one noun is "amor leal". Readable names the women's kindness separately, as the English Readable does, so it is "bondade leal", and the wish is "do mesmo modo ... o seu amor leal", which keeps the comparison.

decisions.choice: vocês; você (Naomi and her daughters-in-law)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Naomi speaks to her daughters-in-law with "vocês" and "você", and Ruth and Orpah answer her with "você", the ordinary address between people (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4). Ruth says "o senhor" to Boaz, a landowner and her superior, and Boaz says "você" and "minha filha" to her (2:8). The masculine plural forms of the Hebrew (m4) need nothing in Portuguese, where "vocês" has no gender.

decisions.choice: may the LORD grant you that you find rest: a wish in short form
alternatives: may the LORD give you husbands, and may you find rest
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "may the LORD give to you, and find rest": what the LORD is to give is the finding of rest itself. Some read an unspoken object ("give you husbands"), but the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: rest: a settled, secure home
decisions.reason: "Rest" here is the security of a home and a husband after the losses of widowhood. Naomi seeks the same "rest" for Ruth in Israel later (3:1).

decisions.choice: lifted their voice and wept: cried aloud
decisions.reason: Raising the voice and weeping is open, loud grief (Genesis 21:16; 29:11), here the grief of parting.

decisions.choice: a new husband (Balanced); a husband and a safe, settled home (Readable)
decisions.reason: Their first husbands are dead, so the "house of her husband" is a new marriage; Balanced says "new". Readable spells out what "rest" in a husband's house means.

decisions.choice: wept aloud; kissed them goodbye, cried loudly
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what lifting the voice means; Readable adds "goodbye", since this is a farewell kiss.

decisions.choice: descanso
decisions.reason: "Descanso" is rest in the sense of m2, a settled life after loss, and it is the word Naomi uses again for Ruth in 3:1, so the two wishes stay linked; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

es.R: Pero ellas le dijeron: «¡No! Nos iremos contigo a tu pueblo».

fr.B: Elles lui dirent : « Non ! Nous retournerons avec toi vers ton peuple. »
fr.R: Mais elles lui ont dit : « Non ! Nous allons avec toi vers ton peuple. »

vi.B: Họ nói với bà: "Không! Chúng con sẽ cùng mẹ trở về với dân của mẹ."

ko.L: 그들이 나오미에게 말했다. "아니에요. 우리는 어머님과 함께 어머님의 백성에게로 돌아가겠어요."

ko.R: 그러나 그들이 나오미에게 말했다. "아니에요! 우리도 어머님과 함께 어머님의 백성에게로 가겠어요."

pt.L: E elas lhe disseram: "Não, com você voltaremos para o seu povo."
pt.B: Elas lhe responderam: "Não! Nós vamos voltar com você para o seu povo."
pt.R: Mas elas disseram: "Não! Nós vamos com você para o seu povo."

decisions.choice: no: rather, a refusal
alternatives: surely we will return with you
decisions.reason: The small word that opens their answer here sets what follows against Naomi's command: not what she says, but this. It is a refusal, "No, we will return with you."

decisions.choice: we will return: going with Naomi as if going home
decisions.reason: The young women use Naomi's word "return" for a land they have never seen. They speak as if her people were already theirs.

decisions.choice: go with you
decisions.reason: "Go back" would puzzle a new reader, since they had never been in Judah; Readable says "go". Literal and Balanced keep the return.

source.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר נָעֳמִי֙ שֹׁ֣בְנָה בְנֹתַ֔י לָ֥מָּה תֵלַ֖כְנָה עִמִּ֑י הַֽעֽוֹד־לִ֤י בָנִים֙ בְּֽמֵעַ֔י וְהָי֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם לַאֲנָשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Naomi, return, my daughters; why will you go with me? [Are there] still to me sons in my inward parts, and they will be for you for husbands?

en.L: And Naomi said, "Return, my daughters. Why would you go with me? Are there still sons in my womb, that they might become husbands for you?
en.B: But Naomi said, "Turn back, my daughters. Why go with me? Do I still have sons inside my womb who could become your husbands?
en.R: Naomi answered, "Go back home, my daughters. Why should you come with me? I cannot give birth to more sons who could become your husbands.

sw.L: Naye Naomi akasema, "Rudini, binti zangu. Kwa nini mwende pamoja nami? Je, bado nina wana tumboni mwangu, ili wawe waume zenu?
sw.B: Lakini Naomi alisema, "Rudini, binti zangu. Kwa nini mwende pamoja nami? Je, bado nina wana tumboni ambao wangeweza kuwa waume zenu?
sw.R: Naomi alijibu, "Rudini nyumbani, binti zangu. Kwa nini mje pamoja nami? Siwezi tena kuzaa wana wengine ambao wangeweza kuwa waume zenu.

es.L: Y dijo Noemí: «{{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}}, hijas mías. ¿Para qué {{plural_you:irían|iríais}} conmigo? ¿Tengo aún hijos en mis entrañas que puedan ser {{plural_you:sus maridos|vuestros maridos}}?
es.B: Pero Noemí dijo: «{{plural_you:Regresen|Regresad}}, hijas mías. ¿Para qué {{plural_you:van a venir|vais a venir}} conmigo? ¿Acaso tengo todavía hijos en mi vientre que puedan llegar a ser {{plural_you:sus maridos|vuestros maridos}}?
es.R: Noemí les contestó: «{{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}} a casa, hijas mías. ¿Para qué {{plural_you:vendrían|vendríais}} conmigo? Ya no puedo tener más hijos que se casen con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}.

fr.L: Et Noémi dit : « Retournez, mes filles. Pourquoi viendriez-vous avec moi ? Ai-je encore des fils dans mes entrailles, qui deviendraient vos maris ?
fr.B: Mais Noémi dit : « Retournez, mes filles. Pourquoi venir avec moi ? Ai-je encore dans mon ventre des fils qui pourraient devenir vos maris ?
fr.R: Noémi a répondu : « Rentrez chez vous, mes filles. Pourquoi venir avec moi ? Je ne peux plus avoir d’autres fils qui pourraient devenir vos maris.

vi.L: Na-ô-mi nói: "Hãy trở về đi, các con gái của mẹ. Sao các con lại đi với mẹ? Trong lòng mẹ còn có con trai để làm chồng các con sao?
vi.B: Nhưng Na-ô-mi nói: "Hãy quay về đi, các con gái của mẹ. Sao lại đi với mẹ? Mẹ còn có con trai trong lòng để làm chồng các con sao?
vi.R: Na-ô-mi trả lời: "Hãy về nhà đi, các con gái của mẹ. Sao các con lại đi với mẹ? Mẹ không thể sinh thêm con trai để làm chồng các con nữa.

ko.L: 나오미가 말했다. "돌아가거라, 내 딸들아. 어찌하여 나와 함께 가려고 하느냐? 내 태 속에 아직 아들들이 있어서 그들이 너희의 남편이 될 수 있겠느냐?
ko.B: 그러나 나오미가 말했다. "돌아가거라, 내 딸들아. 왜 나와 함께 가려고 하느냐? 내 태 속에 아직 아들들이 있어서 너희의 남편이 될 수 있겠느냐?
ko.R: 나오미가 대답했다. "집으로 돌아가거라, 내 딸들아. 왜 나와 함께 가려고 하느냐? 나는 너희의 남편이 될 아들을 더 낳을 수 없다.

pt.L: E Noemi disse: "Voltem, minhas filhas. Por que iriam comigo? Há ainda filhos no meu ventre, para que se tornem maridos de vocês?
pt.B: Mas Noemi disse: "Voltem, minhas filhas. Por que ir comigo? Será que eu ainda tenho filhos no meu ventre, que possam vir a ser maridos de vocês?
pt.R: Noemi respondeu: "Voltem para casa, minhas filhas. Por que vocês viriam comigo? Eu não posso mais dar à luz filhos que venham a ser maridos de vocês.

decisions.choice: sons to become your husbands: the custom of a brother marrying his dead brother's widow
decisions.reason: Naomi's question assumes the custom that when a man died without a son, his brother married the widow to give the dead man a son and an heir (Genesis 38:8; Deuteronomy 25:5-10). Naomi has no more sons to give, so the young women have nothing to hope for in her family. The custom matters again in chapter 4 (4:5, 10).

decisions.choice: my daughters: a word of affection for her daughters-in-law
decisions.reason: Naomi calls her sons' wives "my daughters" (also verses 12-13), and Boaz calls Ruth "my daughter" (2:8). It shows the family bond between them.

decisions.choice: in my inward parts: in my womb
decisions.reason: The word means the inner parts of the body, here the womb (Genesis 25:23).

decisions.choice: a statement in place of the question
decisions.reason: Naomi's question expects the answer no; Readable says it as a plain statement so a young reader does not miss the point.

decisions.choice: Naomi calls the young women "binti zangu" (my daughters) and speaks to them with the plural "ninyi"
decisions.reason: Naomi speaks to them with affection as to daughters (m2), and Swahili, like Hebrew, has its own plural "you", so the address needs no setting.

decisions.choice: "các con gái của mẹ" for "my daughters"
decisions.reason: Naomi calls her daughters-in-law her daughters, a word of affection (meaning decision); Vietnamese keeps it, since "con dâu" would sound cold.

source.text: שֹׁ֤בְנָה בְנֹתַי֙ לֵ֔כְןָ כִּ֥י זָקַ֖נְתִּי מִהְי֣וֹת לְאִ֑ישׁ כִּ֤י אָמַ֨רְתִּי֙ יֶשׁ־לִ֣י תִקְוָ֔ה גַּ֣ם הָיִ֤יתִי הַלַּ֨יְלָה֙ לְאִ֔ישׁ וְגַ֖ם יָלַ֥דְתִּי בָנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Return, my daughters, go, for I am [too] old to be to a husband. If I said, there is to me hope, even [if] I were this night to a husband, and also bore sons,

en.L: Return, my daughters, go, for I am too old to have a husband. If I said, 'I have hope,' even if I had a husband tonight and also bore sons,
en.B: Go back, my daughters, go on your way, for I am too old to marry again. Even if I thought there was still hope for me, even if I had a husband tonight and then gave birth to sons,
en.R: Go back, my daughters. Go! I am too old to marry again. Suppose I told myself there was still hope for me. Suppose I married tonight and later had sons.

sw.L: Rudini, binti zangu, nendeni, kwa maana mimi ni mzee mno kuwa na mume. Kama ningesema, 'Nina tumaini,' hata kama ningekuwa na mume usiku huu, na kuzaa wana pia,
sw.B: Rudini, binti zangu, nendeni zenu, kwa maana mimi ni mzee mno kuolewa tena. Hata kama ningedhani bado nina tumaini, hata kama ningeolewa usiku huu na kisha kuzaa wana,
sw.R: Rudini, binti zangu. Nendeni! Mimi ni mzee mno kuolewa tena. Tuseme ningejiambia kwamba bado nina tumaini. Tuseme ningeolewa usiku huu na baadaye kuzaa wana.

es.L: {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}}, hijas mías, {{plural_you:váyanse|idos}}, porque soy demasiado vieja para tener marido. Si dijera: “Tengo esperanza”, aunque esta noche tuviera marido, y aun diera a luz hijos,
es.B: {{plural_you:Regresen|Regresad}}, hijas mías, {{plural_you:sigan|seguid}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} camino, porque soy demasiado vieja para volver a casarme. Aunque pensara que todavía hay esperanza para mí, aunque esta misma noche tuviera marido y luego diera a luz hijos,
es.R: {{plural_you:Vuelvan|Volved}}, hijas mías. ¡{{plural_you:Váyanse|Idos}}! Ya soy demasiado vieja para volver a casarme. Supongamos que pensara que todavía hay esperanza para mí. Supongamos que me casara esta noche y después tuviera hijos.

fr.L: Retournez, mes filles, allez, car je suis trop vieille pour être à un mari. Si je disais : “J’ai de l’espoir”, même si j’étais cette nuit à un mari et que j’enfantais aussi des fils,
fr.B: Retournez, mes filles, allez-vous-en, car je suis trop vieille pour me remarier. Même si je pensais avoir encore de l’espoir, même si j’avais un mari cette nuit et que je mettais ensuite au monde des fils,
fr.R: Rentrez, mes filles. Allez ! Je suis trop vieille pour me remarier. Imaginez que je me dise qu’il y a encore de l’espoir pour moi. Imaginez que je me marie ce soir et que j’aie ensuite des fils.

vi.L: Hãy trở về đi, các con gái của mẹ, hãy đi đi, vì mẹ đã quá già, không lấy chồng được nữa. Dù mẹ có nói: 'Mẹ còn hy vọng,' dù đêm nay mẹ có chồng và sinh được con trai,
vi.B: Hãy quay về đi, các con gái của mẹ, hãy đi đi, vì mẹ đã quá già, không lấy chồng được nữa. Dù mẹ có nghĩ mình còn hy vọng, dù đêm nay mẹ có chồng rồi sinh được con trai,
vi.R: Hãy quay về đi, các con gái của mẹ. Đi đi! Mẹ đã quá già, không lấy chồng được nữa. Giả sử mẹ tự nhủ rằng mình vẫn còn hy vọng. Giả sử đêm nay mẹ lấy chồng và sau này sinh được con trai.

ko.L: 돌아가거라, 내 딸들아. 가거라. 나는 너무 늙어서 남편을 둘 수 없다. 설령 내가 '나에게 아직 희망이 있다' 하고 말하여, 오늘 밤 내가 남편을 맞아 아들들을 낳는다 하더라도,
ko.B: 돌아가거라, 내 딸들아. 너희 길을 가거라. 나는 너무 늙어서 다시 결혼할 수 없다. 설령 나에게 아직 희망이 있다고 생각하여, 오늘 밤 남편을 맞아 아들들을 낳는다 하더라도,
ko.R: 돌아가거라, 내 딸들아. 어서 가거라! 나는 너무 늙어서 다시 결혼할 수 없다. 내가 나에게 아직 희망이 있다고 생각한다고 하자. 내가 오늘 밤 결혼해서 나중에 아들들을 낳는다고 하자.

pt.L: Voltem, minhas filhas, vão, porque estou velha demais para ter marido. Se eu dissesse: 'Tenho esperança', mesmo que eu tivesse um marido esta noite e também desse à luz filhos,
pt.B: Voltem, minhas filhas, sigam o seu caminho, porque estou velha demais para me casar de novo. Mesmo que eu pensasse que ainda há esperança para mim, mesmo que eu tivesse um marido esta noite e depois desse à luz filhos,
pt.R: Voltem, minhas filhas. Vão! Estou velha demais para me casar outra vez. Imaginem que eu dissesse a mim mesma que ainda há esperança. Imaginem que eu me casasse esta noite e depois tivesse filhos.

decisions.choice: if I said ... even if ...: a run of conditions that verse 13 answers
decisions.reason: Naomi piles up impossible conditions ("if I said I had hope, even if I had a husband tonight, and even if I bore sons") and only gives her answer in verse 13: they could not wait that long. The sentence runs into the next verse.

decisions.choice: to be to a husband: to marry, to be a man's wife
decisions.reason: "To be to a man" means to become a man's wife (Leviticus 21:3; Deuteronomy 24:2). In the second use, "this night", it means to be with a husband at once.

decisions.choice: this night: tonight, at once
decisions.reason: Naomi imagines the quickest case possible: marrying this very night. Even then sons would come far too late.

decisions.choice: Suppose ... Suppose ...
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long chain of conditions into short sentences beginning "Suppose"; verse 13 gives the answer.

source.text: הֲלָהֵ֣ן׀תְּשַׂבֵּ֗רְנָה עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִגְדָּ֔לוּ הֲלָהֵן֙ תֵּֽעָגֵ֔נָה לְבִלְתִּ֖י הֱי֣וֹת לְאִ֑ישׁ אַ֣ל בְּנֹתַ֗י כִּֽי־מַר־לִ֤י מְאֹד֙ מִכֶּ֔ם כִּֽי־יָצְאָ֥ה בִ֖י יַד־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: therefore would you wait until that they grew up? therefore would you shut yourselves off so as not to be to a husband? No, my daughters, for [it is] bitter to me very [much] more than you, for has gone out against me [the] hand of YHWH.

en.L: would you therefore wait until they grew up? Would you therefore shut yourselves away so as not to have a husband? No, my daughters, for it is far more bitter for me than for you, for the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has gone out against me."
en.B: would you then wait until they had grown up? Would you then keep yourselves from marrying? No, my daughters! My lot is far more bitter than yours, for the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has turned against me."

No, hijas mías, porque [es] mucho más amargo para mí que para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotras}}, pues la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se ha levantado contra mí».
es.B: ¿{{plural_you:Esperarían|Esperaríais}} entonces hasta que fueran mayores? ¿{{plural_you:Renunciarían|Renunciaríais}} entonces a {{plural_you:casarse|casaros}}? ¡No, hijas mías! Mi suerte es mucho más amarga que la {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}, porque la mano {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} se ha vuelto contra mí».
es.R: ¿{{plural_you:Esperarían|Esperaríais}} a que crecieran? ¿{{plural_you:Se quedarían|Os quedaríais}} sin casar todo ese tiempo? No, hijas mías. Mi vida es mucho más amarga que la {{plural_you:suya|vuestra}}, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha vuelto {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano contra mí».

fr.L: les attendriez-vous donc jusqu’à ce qu’ils aient grandi ? Vous priveriez-vous donc pour cela d’être à un mari ? Non, mes filles, car c’est bien plus amer pour moi que pour vous, car la main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’est levée contre moi. »
fr.B: les attendriez-vous alors jusqu’à ce qu’ils soient grands ? Renonceriez-vous pour cela à vous marier ? Non, mes filles ! Mon sort est bien plus amer que le vôtre, car la main {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} s’est tournée contre moi. »
fr.R: Est-ce que vous les attendriez jusqu’à ce qu’ils soient grands ? Est-ce que vous resteriez sans mari pendant tout ce temps ? Non, mes filles. Ma vie est bien plus amère que la vôtre, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a levé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main contre moi. »

vi.L: thì các con có chờ cho đến khi chúng lớn lên sao? Các con có vì thế mà giữ mình không lấy chồng sao? Không, các con gái của mẹ, vì mẹ cay đắng hơn các con nhiều lắm, vì tay của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giơ ra chống lại mẹ."
vi.B: thì các con có chờ cho đến khi chúng lớn lên sao? Các con có vì thế mà không lấy chồng sao? Không đâu, các con gái của mẹ! Phần mẹ cay đắng hơn các con nhiều, vì tay của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã chống lại mẹ."
vi.R: Các con có chờ cho chúng lớn lên không? Các con có ở vậy suốt thời gian ấy không? Không đâu, các con gái của mẹ. Đời mẹ cay đắng hơn các con nhiều, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giơ tay {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra chống lại mẹ."

ko.L: 너희가 그들이 자랄 때까지 기다리겠느냐? 그 때문에 너희가 남편을 두지 않고 스스로를 가두어 두겠느냐? 아니다, 내 딸들아. 나는 너희보다 훨씬 더 괴롭다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 손이 나를 치셨기 때문이다."

pt.B: vocês esperariam então até que eles crescessem? Vocês deixariam então de se casar? Não, minhas filhas! A minha sorte é muito mais amarga que a de vocês, porque a mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} se voltou contra mim."
pt.R: Vocês iam esperar até eles crescerem? Iam ficar sem se casar todo esse tempo? Não, minhas filhas. A minha vida é muito mais amarga que a de vocês, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} levantou a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão contra mim."

decisions.choice: therefore: then, in that case
decisions.reason: The short word that opens both questions is best read as "therefore" or "then", as in Aramaic. Others read it as "for them" ("would you wait for them?"); the question is the same either way.

decisions.choice: shut yourselves off: hold back from marriage
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here in the Bible. From related words it means to be kept back or shut in, here kept from marrying, living as a widow with no husband.

decisions.choice: it is far more bitter for me than for you
alternatives: it is very bitter for me because of you
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a comparison ("more bitter for me than for you": the young women can still marry, Naomi cannot) or as "it is very bitter for me because of you" (she grieves over what has happened to them). The comparison fits what follows, that the LORD's hand is against her.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD has gone out against me
decisions.reason: The LORD's hand is his power at work, here in judgment or hardship (Exodus 9:3; Deuteronomy 2:15; Judges 2:15). Naomi sees her losses as coming from the LORD himself. She says it more strongly in verses 20-21; the story does not take back her complaint, but it goes on to show the LORD's care.

decisions.choice: My lot (Balanced); My life (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "it is bitter for me"; Balanced and Readable name what is bitter.

decisions.choice: amargo, amarga
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the word "bitter" here, because Naomi takes it up in her new name, Mara, and in "tornou a minha vida muito amarga" (verses 20-21); "triste" or "difícil" would break the link the meaning note traces.

records.literal_gloss: And they lifted their voice and wept again; and kissed Orpah her mother-in-law, and Ruth clung to her.

en.L: And they lifted up their voices and wept again. And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
en.B: Again they wept aloud. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
en.R: The women cried loudly again. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye and left. But Ruth held on tight to Naomi.

sw.L: Nao wakapaza sauti zao, wakalia tena. Naye Orpa akambusu mama mkwe wake, lakini Ruthu akaambatana naye.
sw.B: Walilia tena kwa sauti kubwa. Kisha Orpa alimbusu mama mkwe wake kumwaga, lakini Ruthu alishikamana naye.
sw.R: Wale wanawake walilia tena kwa sauti kubwa. Kisha Orpa alimbusu mama mkwe wake kumwaga, akaondoka. Lakini Ruthu alimshika Naomi kwa nguvu.

es.L: Y alzaron su voz y lloraron otra vez. Y Orfa besó a su suegra, pero Rut se quedó pegada a ella.
es.B: Otra vez lloraron a gritos. Luego Orfa se despidió de su suegra con un beso, pero Rut se aferró a ella.
es.R: Las mujeres volvieron a llorar a gritos. Entonces Orfa le dio un beso de despedida a su suegra y se fue. Pero Rut se agarró con fuerza a Noemí.

fr.L: Et elles élevèrent la voix et pleurèrent encore. Et Orpa embrassa sa belle-mère, mais Ruth s’attacha à elle.
fr.B: Elles éclatèrent de nouveau en sanglots. Puis Orpa embrassa sa belle-mère pour lui dire adieu, mais Ruth resta attachée à elle.
fr.R: Les femmes se sont remises à pleurer très fort. Ensuite, Orpa a embrassé sa belle-mère pour lui dire au revoir, et elle est partie. Mais Ruth a serré Noémi très fort et ne l’a pas lâchée.

vi.L: Họ lại cất tiếng khóc. Ọt-ba hôn mẹ chồng mình, nhưng Ru-tơ bám lấy bà.
vi.B: Họ lại khóc òa lên. Rồi Ọt-ba hôn từ biệt mẹ chồng, nhưng Ru-tơ cứ níu lấy bà.
vi.R: Các bà lại khóc lớn. Rồi Ọt-ba hôn từ biệt mẹ chồng và ra đi. Nhưng Ru-tơ cứ ôm chặt lấy Na-ô-mi.

ko.L: 그들이 다시 소리 높여 울었다. 오르바는 시어머니에게 입을 맞추었으나, 룻은 그에게 꼭 붙어 있었다.
ko.B: 그들은 다시 소리 내어 울었다. 그리고 오르바는 시어머니에게 작별의 입맞춤을 하였으나, 룻은 시어머니를 붙잡고 놓지 않았다.
ko.R: 그들은 다시 큰 소리로 울었다. 그리고 오르바는 시어머니에게 작별의 입맞춤을 하고 떠났다. 그러나 룻은 나오미를 꼭 붙잡고 놓지 않았다.

pt.L: E elas levantaram a voz e choraram de novo. E Orfa beijou a sua sogra, mas Rute se apegou a ela.
pt.B: De novo elas choraram em alta voz. Então Orfa deu um beijo de despedida na sogra, mas Rute se agarrou a ela.
pt.R: As mulheres choraram alto outra vez. Depois Orfa deu um beijo de despedida na sogra e foi embora. Mas Rute ficou agarrada a Noemi.

decisions.choice: Orpah kissed her mother-in-law: a farewell
decisions.reason: A kiss on parting was a goodbye (Genesis 31:28; 1 Kings 19:20). Orpah does as Naomi asks and goes home; the text does not blame her (Naomi wished her well in verses 8-9).

decisions.choice: clung: held fast, a word for lasting loyalty
decisions.reason: The verb means to stick to or hold fast. It is used of a man holding to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and of Israel holding to the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:20). Ruth's act says what her words in verses 16-17 then put into an oath.

decisions.choice: but Ruth: the two women set side by side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts Ruth's name before the verb, setting her against Orpah: one kissed and left, the other held on.

decisions.choice: goodbye (Balanced, Readable); and left (Readable)
decisions.reason: The kiss is a farewell, and verse 15 says Orpah has gone back; Readable says so here.

decisions.choice: "bám lấy" (L), "níu lấy" (B), "ôm chặt lấy" (R) for "clung"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is used of lasting loyalty, as of a husband to his wife in Genesis 2:24 (meaning decision); each level keeps a verb of holding fast.

decisions.choice: se apegou (L); se agarrou (B); ficou agarrada (R)
decisions.reason: Literal says "apegar-se", the verb for holding fast in loyalty (m2: Genesis 2:24; Deuteronomy 10:20). Balanced and Readable show the act itself, Ruth holding on to Naomi, as the English "held on" does; her words in verses 16-17 then say what the act means.

records.literal_gloss: And she said, look, has returned your sister-in-law to her people and to her gods; return after your sister-in-law.

en.L: And she said, "Look, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods. Return after your sister-in-law."
en.B: Naomi said, "See, your sister-in-law has turned back, home to her people and her gods. Follow your sister-in-law back."
en.R: Naomi said, "Look! Your sister-in-law has gone back to her own people and her own gods. You should go back with her."

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Tazama, wifi yako amerudi kwa watu wake na kwa miungu yake. Rudi umfuate wifi yako."
sw.B: Naomi alisema, "Tazama, wifi yako amerudi nyumbani kwa watu wake na kwa miungu yake. Mfuate wifi yako urudi."
sw.R: Naomi alisema, "Tazama! Wifi yako amerudi kwa watu wake mwenyewe na kwa miungu yake mwenyewe. Nawe unapaswa kurudi pamoja naye."

es.L: Y ella dijo: «He aquí, tu cuñada se ha vuelto a su pueblo y a sus dioses; vuélvete tú tras tu cuñada».
es.B: Noemí le dijo: «Mira, tu cuñada se vuelve a su pueblo y a sus dioses. Vuélvete tú también con ella».
es.R: Noemí le dijo: «¡Mira! Tu cuñada se ha vuelto a su propio pueblo y a sus propios dioses. Tú deberías volverte con ella».

fr.B: Noémi lui dit : « Tu vois, ta belle-sœur est retournée vers son peuple et vers ses dieux. Retourne, toi aussi, à la suite de ta belle-sœur. »
fr.R: Noémi a dit : « Regarde ! Ta belle-sœur est retournée chez son peuple et chez ses dieux. Tu devrais repartir avec elle. »

vi.L: Bà nói: "Này, chị dâu con đã trở về với dân mình và các thần của mình. Con hãy trở về theo chị dâu con đi."
vi.B: Na-ô-mi nói: "Kìa, chị dâu con đã quay về với dân mình và các thần của mình. Con cũng hãy theo chị dâu mà về đi."

ko.B: 나오미가 말했다. "보아라, 네 동서는 자기 백성과 자기 신들에게로 돌아갔다. 너도 동서를 따라 돌아가거라."

pt.B: Noemi disse: "Veja, a sua cunhada voltou para casa, para o povo e para os deuses dela. Volte você também, atrás da sua cunhada."
pt.R: Noemi disse: "Olhe! A sua cunhada voltou para o povo dela e para os deuses dela. Você deveria voltar com ela."

decisions.choice: her gods: the gods of Moab
decisions.reason: The plural word can mean "gods" or, of Israel's God, "God". Here it is the god or gods of Moab, chiefly Chemosh (Numbers 21:29; 1 Kings 11:33). Going home meant going back to Moab's worship as well; Ruth's answer in verse 16 turns on this.

decisions.choice: sister-in-law: the widow of her husband's brother
decisions.reason: The word is used for the wife of one's husband's brother, the same family word found in the law of a brother's widow (Deuteronomy 25:7, 9).

decisions.choice: Naomi said
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "she said"; Balanced and Readable name Naomi so the speaker is clear.

decisions.choice: "chị dâu" for "sister-in-law"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say whether a sister-in-law is older or younger; Orpah is named first in verse 4, so she is taken as the elder. The Hebrew does not say.

decisions.choice: a sua cunhada
decisions.reason: "Cunhada" is the everyday word for the wife of one's husband's brother, and it is the word Deuteronomy 25:7, 9 uses in Portuguese for the same Hebrew (m2), the feminine of "o cunhado". "Concunhada" is precise but rare. "Dela" in place of "seu" makes clear that the people and the gods are Orpah's.
