records.literal_gloss: And said Ruth, do not urge me to leave you, to turn back from after you; for to where you go I will go, and in where you lodge I will lodge; your people my people, and your God my God.

en.L: And Ruth said, "Do not press me to abandon you, to turn back from following you. For to the place you go, I will go, and in the place you lodge, I will lodge. Your people [are] my people, and your God [is] my God.
en.B: But Ruth said, "Stop pressing me to leave you and turn away from following you. Wherever you travel, I will travel with you; wherever you stop for the night, I will stop as well. Your people are now my people, and your God is now my God.
en.R: But Ruth answered, "Do not ask me to leave you or to turn back and stop following you. I am going with you, wherever that takes me. Wherever you sleep, I will sleep too. From now on your people are my people, and your God is my God.

sw.L: Naye Ruthu akasema, "Usinishurutishe nikuache, nigeuke nisikufuate. Kwa maana mahali utakapokwenda, nami nitakwenda huko, na mahali utakapolala, nami nitalala huko. Watu wako [ni] watu wangu, na Mungu wako [ni] Mungu wangu.
sw.B: Lakini Ruthu alisema, "Acha kunibana niachane nawe na kugeuka nisiendelee kukufuata. Popote utakaposafiri, nitasafiri pamoja nawe; popote utakapolala usiku, nitalala pia. Watu wako sasa ni watu wangu, na Mungu wako sasa ni Mungu wangu.
sw.R: Lakini Ruthu alijibu, "Usiniombe nikuache wala nirudi nisiendelee kukufuata. Ninakwenda pamoja nawe, popote itakaponifikisha. Popote utakapolala, nami nitalala. Kuanzia sasa watu wako ni watu wangu, na Mungu wako ni Mungu wangu.

es.L: Y dijo Rut: «No me presiones a abandonarte, a volverme de seguirte. Porque al lugar adonde tú vayas, iré yo, y en el lugar donde pases la noche, pasaré yo la noche. Tu pueblo [es] mi pueblo, y tu Dios [es] mi Dios.
es.B: Pero Rut le dijo: «Deja ya de insistirme en que te abandone y me aparte de ti. Adondequiera que viajes, viajaré contigo; dondequiera que te detengas a pasar la noche, allí me detendré yo también. Tu pueblo es ahora mi pueblo, y tu Dios es ahora mi Dios.
es.R: Pero Rut le contestó: «No me pidas que te deje ni que me dé la vuelta y deje de seguirte. Yo me voy contigo, adondequiera que eso me lleve. Donde tú duermas, dormiré yo también. Desde ahora tu pueblo es mi pueblo, y tu Dios es mi Dios.

fr.L: Et Ruth dit : « Ne me presse pas de t’abandonner, de m’en retourner loin de toi. Car là où tu iras, j’irai, et là où tu passeras la nuit, je passerai la nuit. Ton peuple [est] mon peuple, et ton Dieu [est] mon Dieu.
fr.B: Mais Ruth répondit : « Cesse d’insister pour que je te quitte et que je cesse de te suivre. Partout où tu iras, j’irai avec toi ; partout où tu t’arrêteras pour la nuit, je m’arrêterai aussi. Ton peuple est désormais mon peuple, et ton Dieu est désormais mon Dieu.
fr.R: Mais Ruth a répondu : « Ne me demande pas de te laisser ou de faire demi-tour et de ne plus te suivre. Je viens avec toi, où que tu ailles. Là où tu dormiras, je dormirai aussi. À partir de maintenant, ton peuple est mon peuple, et ton Dieu est mon Dieu.

vi.L: Ru-tơ nói: "Xin mẹ đừng nài ép con lìa bỏ mẹ, quay về không theo mẹ nữa. Vì mẹ đi đến đâu, con sẽ đi đến đó; mẹ nghỉ đêm ở đâu, con sẽ nghỉ đêm ở đó. Dân của mẹ [là] dân của con, và Đức Chúa Trời của mẹ [là] Đức Chúa Trời của con.
vi.B: Nhưng Ru-tơ nói: "Xin mẹ thôi nài ép con bỏ mẹ mà quay về, không theo mẹ nữa. Mẹ đi đến đâu, con sẽ cùng đi đến đó; mẹ dừng chân nghỉ đêm ở đâu, con cũng sẽ nghỉ ở đó. Từ nay dân của mẹ là dân của con, và Đức Chúa Trời của mẹ là Đức Chúa Trời của con.
vi.R: Nhưng Ru-tơ trả lời: "Xin mẹ đừng bảo con bỏ mẹ, hay quay về mà không theo mẹ nữa. Con sẽ đi với mẹ, dù đi đến bất cứ nơi đâu. Mẹ ngủ ở đâu, con cũng sẽ ngủ ở đó. Từ nay trở đi, dân của mẹ là dân của con, và Đức Chúa Trời của mẹ là Đức Chúa Trời của con.

ko.L: 룻이 말했다. "어머님을 버리고 어머님을 따르지 말고 돌아가라고 저를 조르지 마세요. 어머님이 가실 그곳으로 저도 가겠고, 어머님이 밤을 지내실 그곳에서 저도 밤을 지내겠어요. 어머님의 백성이 곧 제 백성이고, 어머님의 하나님이 곧 제 하나님이세요.
ko.B: 그러나 룻이 말했다. "어머님 곁을 떠나 돌아가라고 더는 저를 조르지 마세요. 어머님이 길을 가시면 어디든지 저도 함께 가겠어요. 어머님이 어디에서 밤을 지내시든지 저도 거기에서 지내겠어요. 이제 어머님의 백성은 제 백성이고, 어머님의 하나님은 제 하나님이에요.
ko.R: 그러나 룻이 대답했다. "어머님을 떠나라고 하지 마세요. 돌아가서 어머님을 따르지 말라고 하지 마세요. 어디로 가시든지 저는 어머님과 함께 가겠어요. 어머님이 주무시는 곳에서 저도 자겠어요. 이제부터 어머님의 백성이 제 백성이고, 어머님의 하나님이 제 하나님이에요.

pt.L: E Rute disse: "Não insista comigo para que eu a deixe, para que eu volte e não a siga. Pois aonde você for, eu irei, e onde você passar a noite, eu passarei a noite. O seu povo [é] o meu povo, e o seu Deus [é] o meu Deus.
pt.B: Mas Rute respondeu: "Pare de insistir para que eu a abandone e deixe de seguir você. Para onde você for, eu vou; onde você parar para passar a noite, ali eu também vou parar. O seu povo agora é o meu povo, e o seu Deus agora é o meu Deus.
pt.R: Mas Rute respondeu: "Não me peça para deixar você, nem para voltar e parar de seguir você. Para onde você for, eu vou com você. Onde você dormir, eu também vou dormir. De agora em diante o seu povo é o meu povo, e o seu Deus é o meu Deus.

decisions.choice: urge me: press me with requests
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet someone, and so to press them with a request (Genesis 23:8). Naomi has urged her three times (verses 8, 11-13, 15); Ruth asks her to stop.

decisions.choice: lodge: spend the night
decisions.reason: The verb means to stay for the night. On the road it is each night's stop; beyond the road it is wherever Naomi will live.

decisions.choice: your people my people, and your God my God: a declaration with no verb
alternatives: your people will be my people, and your God will be my God
decisions.reason: Hebrew can join two nouns with no verb between them. Ruth's words state what is true from this moment and for the future: she belongs to Naomi's people and takes Naomi's God as her own. The pledge is built from short balanced pairs, ending in the oath of verse 17.

decisions.choice: your God my God: Ruth takes the God of Israel as her own
decisions.reason: Orpah has gone back "to her gods" (verse 15); Ruth chooses the God of Naomi, the LORD, by whose name she swears in verse 17. Boaz later speaks of her as one who has come to take refuge under the LORD's wings (2:12).

decisions.choice: are now (Balanced); From now on (Readable)
decisions.reason: With no verb in the Hebrew, Balanced and Readable say "now" to show the declaration takes effect from this moment; Literal brackets the supplied verb.

decisions.choice: drafted from the Hebrew, with "passer la nuit" for "lodge" (L) and "désormais" (B) for the new belonging
alternatives: the familiar wording of the Segond tradition ("où tu iras j'irai, où tu demeureras je demeurerai")
decisions.reason: As the terms note for these books asks, Ruth 1:16-17 is drafted from the Hebrew and the gloss rather than from the well-known French wording; the short common phrase "là où tu iras, j'irai" is the plain way to say it in French, and the rest is worded afresh.

decisions.choice: Ruth calls herself "con" and Naomi "mẹ"
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note. The verse is drafted from the Hebrew, avoiding the wording of the familiar Vietnamese versions beyond short common phrases.

decisions.choice: Ruth's words drafted from the Hebrew, with "밤을 지내다" for "lodge" and "곧" in the verbless declaration
decisions.reason: This verse is among the best known in the Old Testament; Korean follows the Hebrew line by line and avoids the wording of the familiar Korean versions, as the terms of this translation require.

decisions.choice: aonde você for, eu irei (L); Para onde você for, eu vou (B, R); passar a noite (L, B), dormir (R)
decisions.reason: Drafted from the Hebrew for the whole book: Ruth says "você" to her mother-in-law, as Naomi says "vocês" to her (verse 8). Literal keeps the Hebrew's future, "eu irei"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday present, "eu vou", which also keeps this best-known line clear of published versions. The verb of m2 is spending the night, so Literal and Balanced say "passar a noite" and Readable "dormir"; "pousar" is old-fashioned, and "ficar" or "morar" would lose the picture.

source.text: בַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר תָּמ֨וּתִי֙ אָמ֔וּת וְשָׁ֖ם אֶקָּבֵ֑ר כֹּה֩ יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֔יף כִּ֣י הַמָּ֔וֶת יַפְרִ֖יד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: In where you die I will die, and there I will be buried. Thus may do YHWH to me, and thus may he add, if death will separate between me and between you.

en.L: In the place you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. Thus may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do to me, and more also, if [anything but] death separates me from you."
en.B: The place where you die is where I will die and be buried. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} deal with me ever so severely if anything except death comes between us."
en.R: I will die where you die, and be buried in the same place. I make this solemn promise before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: only death will separate us. If I break it, may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} punish me severely."

sw.L: Mahali utakapokufa ndipo nitakapokufa, na huko nitazikwa. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na anitendee hivyo, na kuongeza zaidi, ikiwa [kitu kingine ila] kifo kitanitenganisha nawe."
sw.B: Mahali utakapokufa ndipo nitakapokufa na kuzikwa. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na aniadhibu vikali kabisa kama kitu chochote isipokuwa kifo kitatutenganisha."
sw.R: Nitakufa pale utakapokufa, na kuzikwa mahali pale pale. Ninaahidi kwa kiapo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: ni kifo tu kitakachotutenganisha. Nikiivunja ahadi hii, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} na aniadhibu vikali."

es.L: En el lugar donde tú mueras, moriré yo, y allí seré sepultada. Así me haga {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y aún más, si [otra cosa que] la muerte me separa de ti».
es.B: Donde tú mueras, allí moriré yo y allí me sepultarán. Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me castigue con toda dureza si algo que no sea la muerte se interpone entre nosotras».
es.R: Moriré donde tú mueras, y me enterrarán en el mismo lugar. Hago esta promesa solemne delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: solo la muerte nos separará. Si no la cumplo, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me castigue con dureza».

fr.L: Là où tu mourras, je mourrai, et là je serai enterrée. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me fasse ainsi, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y ajoute encore, si [autre chose que] la mort me sépare de toi. »
fr.B: Là où tu mourras, je mourrai, et c’est là que je serai enterrée. Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me punisse avec la plus grande sévérité si autre chose que la mort vient nous séparer ! »
fr.R: Je mourrai là où tu mourras, et je serai enterrée au même endroit. Je fais cette promesse solennelle devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : seule la mort nous séparera. Si je ne tiens pas ma promesse, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me punisse sévèrement. »

vi.L: Mẹ chết ở đâu, con sẽ chết ở đó, và con sẽ được chôn ở đó. Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xử với con như vậy, và còn nặng hơn nữa, nếu có [điều gì ngoài] sự chết chia lìa con với mẹ."
vi.B: Mẹ qua đời ở đâu, con cũng sẽ chết và được chôn ở đó. Nếu có điều gì ngoài cái chết chia cách con với mẹ, xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phạt con thật nặng."
vi.R: Mẹ chết ở đâu, con sẽ chết ở đó, và được chôn cùng một nơi. Con xin long trọng hứa trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: chỉ có cái chết mới chia lìa được hai mẹ con mình. Nếu con không giữ lời, xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phạt con thật nặng."

ko.L: 어머님이 돌아가실 그곳에서 저도 죽고, 거기에 저도 묻히겠어요. 죽음 [말고 무엇이든] 저를 어머님에게서 떼어 놓는다면, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 저에게 벌을 내리시고 더 내리셔도 좋아요."
ko.B: 어머님이 돌아가시는 곳에서 저도 죽고, 거기에 묻히겠어요. 죽음 말고 무엇이든 우리 사이를 갈라놓는다면, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 저에게 무거운 벌을 내리셔도 좋아요."
ko.R: 어머님이 돌아가시는 곳에서 저도 죽고, 같은 곳에 묻히겠어요. 저는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 엄숙하게 약속해요. 죽음만이 우리를 떼어 놓을 거예요. 제가 이 약속을 어기면, 그분께서 저에게 무거운 벌을 내리셔도 좋아요."

pt.L: Onde você morrer, eu morrerei, e ali serei sepultada. Assim me faça {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, e mais ainda, se [algo além da] morte me separar de você."
pt.B: Onde você morrer, ali eu vou morrer e ali vou ser sepultada. Que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me trate com toda a dureza, e mais ainda, se alguma coisa além da morte me separar de você."
pt.R: Vou morrer onde você morrer e vou ser sepultada no mesmo lugar. Faço esta promessa solene diante {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}: só a morte vai nos separar. Se eu quebrar esta promessa, que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me castigue duramente."

decisions.choice: there I will be buried: belonging for life and death
decisions.reason: To be buried in a land and with a family was to belong to it for good (Genesis 47:29-30; 50:25). Ruth will not even go back to Moab to be buried.

decisions.choice: thus may the LORD do to me and thus may he add: an oath that calls down a curse on oneself
decisions.reason: This is a set form of oath (1 Samuel 3:17; 2 Samuel 3:9; 1 Kings 19:2). The speaker asks God to punish them, and more besides, if they break their word; the punishment is left unspoken. Ruth swears by the LORD, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: if anything but death separates me from you
alternatives: if even death separates me from you
decisions.reason: After this oath the small word that follows gives what is sworn. It can be read "if anything but death separates us" (only death will part them) or "if even death separates us" (not even death will, since she will be buried beside Naomi). Both make the pledge as strong as possible; the first fits the plain sense of the words best.

decisions.choice: [anything but] (Literal); anything except (Balanced); only death (Readable)
decisions.reason: The words supplied give the reading chosen in m3; Literal brackets them.

decisions.choice: the promise first, then the curse
decisions.reason: Readable says what Ruth promises before the self-curse, and explains the oath form in plain words.

decisions.choice: "Nguyện CHÚA xử với con như vậy, và còn nặng hơn nữa" at Literal
decisions.reason: The form of an oath that calls a curse on oneself (meaning decision); Literal keeps both halves, the other levels say plainly what the curse means.

decisions.choice: Ruth's oath in the polite informal style (해요체) she uses with Naomi
decisions.reason: The oath is spoken to Naomi, with the LORD as witness, so it keeps her speech level to Naomi; Korean says "벌을 내리시다" (punish) for the Hebrew "thus may the LORD do to me".

source.text: וַתֵּ֕רֶא כִּֽי־מִתְאַמֶּ֥צֶת הִ֖יא לָלֶ֣כֶת אִתָּ֑הּ וַתֶּחְדַּ֖ל לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she saw that determined [was] she to go with her, and she ceased to speak to her.

en.L: And she saw that she was determined to go with her, and she stopped speaking to her.
en.B: When Naomi saw that Ruth was set on going with her, she said no more to her.
en.R: Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her. So Naomi stopped arguing with her.

sw.L: Naye alipoona ya kuwa amekaza nia kwenda pamoja naye, akaacha kusema naye.
sw.B: Naomi alipoona kwamba Ruthu ameazimia kwenda pamoja naye, hakusema naye tena.
sw.R: Naomi aliona kwamba Ruthu ameamua kabisa kwenda pamoja naye. Kwa hiyo Naomi aliacha kubishana naye.

es.L: Y vio que estaba resuelta a ir con ella, y dejó de hablarle.
es.B: Cuando Noemí vio que Rut estaba decidida a ir con ella, no le dijo nada más.
es.R: Noemí vio que Rut estaba decidida a ir con ella. Así que dejó de discutir con ella.

fr.L: Et elle vit qu’elle était résolue à aller avec elle, et elle cessa de lui parler.
fr.B: Quand Noémi vit que Ruth était décidée à partir avec elle, elle n’insista plus.
fr.R: Noémi a vu que Ruth avait pris sa décision de partir avec elle. Alors Noémi a arrêté de discuter avec elle.

vi.L: Bà thấy nàng nhất quyết đi với mình, thì thôi không nói với nàng nữa.
vi.B: Khi Na-ô-mi thấy Ru-tơ nhất quyết đi với mình, bà không nói gì thêm nữa.
vi.R: Na-ô-mi thấy Ru-tơ đã quyết tâm đi với mình. Vậy Na-ô-mi thôi không cãi với nàng nữa.

ko.L: 나오미는 룻이 자기와 함께 가기로 굳게 마음먹은 것을 보고, 그에게 더 말하지 않았다.
ko.B: 나오미는 룻이 자기와 함께 가기로 굳게 결심한 것을 보고, 더는 말리지 않았다.
ko.R: 나오미는 룻이 자기와 함께 가기로 마음을 굳힌 것을 알았다. 그래서 나오미는 더는 룻을 말리지 않았다.

pt.L: E ela viu que ela estava decidida a ir com ela, e deixou de falar com ela.
pt.B: Quando Noemi viu que Rute estava firme em ir com ela, não lhe disse mais nada.
pt.R: Noemi viu que Rute estava decidida a ir com ela. Então Noemi parou de discutir com ela.

decisions.choice: determined: had made herself firm
decisions.reason: The verb means to make oneself strong or firm; here Ruth's mind is set and cannot be moved (compare 2 Chronicles 13:7).

decisions.choice: she stopped speaking to her: Naomi ended her pleading
decisions.reason: Naomi stops urging Ruth to go back. Nothing is said of her answer; she says no word to Ruth until they reach Bethlehem, and there she speaks as if she had come home "empty" (verse 21).

decisions.choice: Naomi ... Ruth
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "she" and "her"; Balanced and Readable name the two women.

decisions.choice: stopped arguing with her
decisions.reason: Readable says what Naomi's speaking had been: trying to persuade Ruth to go back.

decisions.choice: The narrative calls Ruth "nàng" and Naomi "bà"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese narration needs pronouns for both women; "nàng" for the young widow and "bà" for the older woman, as Genesis uses "nàng" for young women.

source.text: וַתֵּלַ֣כְנָה שְׁתֵּיהֶ֔ם עַד־בֹּאָ֖נָה בֵּ֣ית לָ֑חֶם וַיְהִ֗י כְּבֹאָ֨נָה֙ בֵּ֣ית לֶ֔חֶם וַתֵּהֹ֤ם כָּל־הָעִיר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ן וַתֹּאמַ֖רְנָה הֲזֹ֥את נָעֳמִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went, [the] two of them, until they came [to] Bethlehem. And it was, as they came [to] Bethlehem, and was stirred all the town over them, and they said, [is] this Naomi?

en.L: And the two of them went on until they came to Bethlehem. And it happened, as they came to Bethlehem, that the whole town was stirred over them, and they said, "Is this Naomi?"
en.B: So the two of them traveled on until they reached Bethlehem. When they arrived, the whole town was in an uproar over them, and the women said, "Can this be Naomi?"
en.R: The two women walked on until they reached Bethlehem. When they arrived, the whole town was excited about them. The women there asked, "Is this really Naomi?"

sw.L: Nao wakaenda wote wawili mpaka wakafika Bethlehemu. Ikawa walipofika Bethlehemu, mji wote ukataharuki kwa ajili yao, wakasema, "Je, huyu ni Naomi?"
sw.B: Basi wote wawili walisafiri mpaka wakafika Bethlehemu. Walipofika, mji wote ukataharuki kwa ajili yao, na wanawake wakasema, "Je, kweli huyu ni Naomi?"
sw.R: Wale wanawake wawili walitembea mpaka wakafika Bethlehemu. Walipofika, mji wote ulifurahi na kushangaa kwa ajili yao. Wanawake wa huko waliuliza, "Kweli huyu ni Naomi?"

es.L: Y anduvieron las dos hasta que llegaron a Belén. Y sucedió que, al llegar a Belén, toda la ciudad se conmovió por causa de ellas, y decían: «¿Es esta Noemí?».
es.B: Así que las dos siguieron caminando hasta llegar a Belén. Cuando llegaron, todo el pueblo se alborotó por ellas, y las mujeres decían: «¿Será esta Noemí?».
es.R: Las dos mujeres siguieron caminando hasta que llegaron a Belén. Cuando llegaron, todo el pueblo se emocionó por ellas. Las mujeres de allí preguntaban: «¿De verdad es esta Noemí?».

fr.L: Et elles allèrent toutes les deux jusqu’à leur arrivée à Bethléem. Et il arriva, quand elles entrèrent à Bethléem, que toute la ville s’agita à leur sujet, et elles disaient : « Est-ce là Noémi ? »
fr.B: Elles marchèrent donc toutes les deux jusqu’à Bethléem. Quand elles arrivèrent, toute la ville fut en émoi à leur sujet, et les femmes disaient : « Est-ce bien Noémi ? »
fr.R: Les deux femmes ont marché jusqu’à Bethléem. Quand elles sont arrivées, toute la ville s’est agitée à cause d’elles. Les femmes demandaient : « C’est vraiment Noémi ? »

vi.L: Hai người đi cho đến khi tới Bết-lê-hem. Khi họ đến Bết-lê-hem, cả thành xôn xao vì họ, và người ta nói: "Đây có phải là Na-ô-mi không?"
vi.B: Vậy hai người tiếp tục đi cho đến khi tới Bết-lê-hem. Khi họ đến nơi, cả thành xôn xao về họ, và các phụ nữ nói: "Đây có phải là Na-ô-mi không?"
vi.R: Hai người đi cho đến khi tới Bết-lê-hem. Khi họ đến nơi, cả thành rộn lên vì họ. Các phụ nữ ở đó hỏi nhau: "Có thật đây là Na-ô-mi không?"

ko.L: 그 두 사람이 길을 가서 베들레헴에 이르렀다. 그들이 베들레헴에 이르자 온 성읍이 그들 때문에 떠들썩하였다. 여자들이 말했다. "이 사람이 나오미가 아니냐?"
ko.B: 그래서 두 사람은 계속 걸어서 베들레헴에 이르렀다. 그들이 베들레헴에 도착하자 온 성읍이 그들 때문에 떠들썩하였다. 여자들이 말했다. "이 사람이 정말 나오미인가?"
ko.R: 두 여자는 계속 걸어서 베들레헴에 이르렀다. 그들이 도착하자 온 성이 그들 때문에 들썩였다. 그곳 여자들이 물었다. "이 사람이 정말 나오미인가?"

pt.L: E as duas foram até chegarem a Belém. E aconteceu que, quando chegaram a Belém, toda a cidade se agitou por causa delas, e elas disseram: "Esta é Noemi?"
pt.B: Assim as duas seguiram viagem até chegarem a Belém. Quando chegaram, a cidade inteira ficou alvoroçada por causa delas, e as mulheres diziam: "Será que esta é Noemi?"
pt.R: As duas mulheres continuaram andando até chegarem a Belém. Quando elas chegaram, a cidade toda ficou agitada por causa delas. As mulheres de lá perguntavam: "Esta é mesmo Noemi?"

decisions.choice: was stirred: was in an uproar
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a crowd or a town in commotion (1 Samuel 4:5; 1 Kings 1:45). Their arrival is the talk of the town; the word does not say whether the stir was joy or shock.

decisions.choice: they said: the women of the town
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine plural: the women of Bethlehem speak. They speak again at the end of the book, when they bless Naomi over her grandson (4:14-17).

decisions.choice: Is this Naomi? astonishment at how she has changed
decisions.reason: The question is surprise rather than a request for her name: after some ten years and her losses, she is hardly the woman they knew. Naomi's answer in verses 20-21 takes it that way.

decisions.choice: the women
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who spoke, as the feminine verb does; Literal keeps "they".

decisions.choice: elas disseram
decisions.reason: Where the English Literal says "they", Portuguese "elas" already shows what the feminine verb shows (m2): the women of the town speak. Balanced and Readable name them, as the English does.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ן אַל־תִּקְרֶ֥אנָה לִ֖י נָעֳמִ֑י קְרֶ֤אןָ לִי֙ מָרָ֔א כִּי־הֵמַ֥ר שַׁדַּ֛י לִ֖י מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to them, do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for has made bitter [the] Almighty to me very [much].

en.L: And she said to them, "Do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
en.B: She said to them, "Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has made my life very bitter.
en.R: Naomi told them, "Do not call me Naomi, which means 'pleasant.' Call me Mara, which means 'bitter.' God All-Powerful has made my life very bitter.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Msiniite Naomi; niiteni Mara, kwa maana Mwenyezi amenitendea kwa uchungu mwingi.
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Msiniite Naomi. Niiteni Mara, kwa maana Mwenyezi ameyafanya maisha yangu kuwa machungu sana.
sw.R: Naomi aliwaambia, "Msiniite Naomi, maana yake 'mpendezaji.' Niiteni Mara, maana yake 'uchungu.' Mungu Mwenyezi ameyafanya maisha yangu kuwa machungu sana.

es.L: Y ella les dijo: «No me {{plural_you:llamen|llaméis}} Noemí; {{plural_you:llámenme|llamadme}} Mara, porque el Todopoderoso me ha tratado con mucha amargura.
es.B: Ella les dijo: «No me {{plural_you:llamen|llaméis}} Noemí. {{plural_you:Llámenme|Llamadme}} Mara, porque el Todopoderoso ha llenado mi vida de amargura.
es.R: Noemí les dijo: «No me {{plural_you:llamen|llaméis}} Noemí, que quiere decir “agradable”. {{plural_you:Llámenme|Llamadme}} Mara, que quiere decir “amarga”. El Dios Todopoderoso ha hecho muy amarga mi vida.

fr.L: Et elle leur dit : « Ne m’appelez pas Noémi ; appelez-moi Mara, car le Tout-Puissant m’a remplie de beaucoup d’amertume.
fr.B: Elle leur dit : « Ne m’appelez plus Noémi. Appelez-moi Mara, car le Tout-Puissant a rendu ma vie très amère.
fr.R: Noémi leur a dit : « Ne m’appelez pas Noémi, ce qui veut dire “agréable”. Appelez-moi Mara, ce qui veut dire “amère”. Dieu le Tout-Puissant a rendu ma vie très amère.

vi.L: Bà nói với họ: "Đừng gọi tôi là Na-ô-mi; hãy gọi tôi là Ma-ra, vì Đấng Toàn Năng đã làm cho tôi rất cay đắng.
vi.B: Bà nói với họ: "Đừng gọi tôi là Na-ô-mi nữa. Hãy gọi tôi là Ma-ra, vì Đấng Toàn Năng đã làm cho đời tôi rất cay đắng.
vi.R: Na-ô-mi nói với họ: "Đừng gọi tôi là Na-ô-mi, nghĩa là 'vui thích.' Hãy gọi tôi là Ma-ra, nghĩa là 'cay đắng.' Đức Chúa Trời Toàn Năng đã làm cho đời tôi rất cay đắng.

ko.L: 나오미가 그들에게 말했다. "나를 나오미라고 부르지 마십시오. 나를 마라라고 부르십시오. 전능자께서 나를 몹시 괴롭게 하셨습니다.
ko.B: 나오미가 그들에게 말했다. "나를 나오미라고 부르지 마십시오. 마라라고 부르십시오. 전능자께서 내 삶을 몹시 괴롭게 하셨습니다.

pt.L: E ela lhes disse: "Não me chamem Noemi; chamem-me Mara, porque o Todo-Poderoso me tratou com muita amargura.
pt.B: Ela lhes respondeu: "Não me chamem de Noemi. Chamem-me de Mara, porque o Todo-Poderoso tornou a minha vida muito amarga.

decisions.choice: Naomi "pleasant", Mara "bitter": a new name for a changed life
decisions.reason: Naomi means "pleasant" or "my pleasantness"; Mara means "bitter", from the same root as "has made bitter" in this verse and "bitter" in verse 13. She asks to be named for what has happened to her. No one in the story calls her Mara; she is Naomi to the end (4:17).

decisions.choice: the Almighty: Shaddai, an ancient name of God
decisions.reason: Shaddai is a very old name for God, used with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Genesis 17:1; Exodus 6:3). Its first meaning is not certain; "the Almighty" is the long-standing sense. In Job it is the name of the God who sends both good and suffering, and Job uses almost Naomi's words: "the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter" (Job 27:2).

decisions.choice: the Almighty has dealt bitterly with me: Naomi lays her loss at God's door
decisions.reason: Naomi does not deny God's rule; she holds to it and complains of it, as Job and many psalms do. The story does not rebuke her; it goes on to show the same God bringing her blessing (4:14-15).

decisions.choice: the Almighty (Literal, Balanced); God All-Powerful (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Numbers, Readable puts the name in plain words.

decisions.choice: which means 'pleasant'; which means 'bitter'
decisions.reason: The point of Naomi's words lies in the meaning of the names; Readable gives it in the text so a reader without a footnote can follow.

decisions.choice: "Mwenyezi" (the Almighty) for Shaddai at Literal and Balanced; "Mungu Mwenyezi" at Readable
decisions.reason: As agreed for Ruth in every language, and as "Mungu Mwenyezi" stands for El Shaddai in Genesis: Readable adds "Mungu" so that a new reader knows who is meant, as the English Readable says "God All-Powerful".

decisions.choice: Readable explains the names: Naomi "mpendezaji" (pleasant one), Mara "uchungu" (bitterness)
decisions.reason: The point of Naomi's words is what the two names mean (m1); Readable says it, as the English Readable does. "Mara" and "machungu" do not sound alike in Swahili, so the explanation carries the wordplay.

decisions.choice: "el Todopoderoso" (L, B); "el Dios Todopoderoso" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for Shaddai, the ancient name of God (m2): "el Todopoderoso" at Literal and Balanced; Readable adds "Dios", as the English Readable says "God All-Powerful", so that a new reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: "le Tout-Puissant" (L, B); "Dieu le Tout-Puissant" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note for these books sets for Shaddai, an ancient name of God (m2): "le Tout-Puissant"; Readable adds "Dieu", as the English Readable says "God All-Powerful". The same in verse 21.

decisions.choice: "Đấng Toàn Năng" (L, B), "Đức Chúa Trời Toàn Năng" (R) for Shaddai
decisions.reason: As the Joshua–Ruth terms note; Readable names God plainly, as the English Readable "God All-Powerful" does, in the form the Genesis note uses for El Shaddai.

decisions.choice: Readable explains the names: "vui thích" and "cay đắng"
decisions.reason: Naomi's words turn on what the two names mean (meaning decision), which a Vietnamese reader cannot hear in the names themselves.

decisions.choice: "전능자" at Literal and Balanced; "전능하신 하나님" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for Shaddai in Ruth.

decisions.choice: Naomi speaks to the women of the town in the formal polite style (합쇼체)
decisions.reason: She speaks to a crowd of neighbours after ten years away, publicly and with some formality; her bitter words are her own, not a change in her standing.

decisions.choice: Mara; amargura (L), amarga (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the name stays "Mara", and the verb that explains it is rendered with "amargo" at every level, as in verse 13. Portuguese hears the same sound in "Mara" and "amarga", so the play of m1 comes through even at Literal; Readable also gives the meaning of both names, as the English Readable does. "Noemi" ("agradável") stays her name to the end of the book.

decisions.choice: o Todo-Poderoso (L, B); o Deus Todo-Poderoso (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (verse 21 too): Shaddai alone is "o Todo-Poderoso", as Numbers 24:4 has it in Portuguese under docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md; Readable adds "Deus", as the English Readable says "God All-Powerful".

es.L: Llena me fui, y vacía me ha hecho volver {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. ¿Por qué me {{plural_you:llaman|llamáis}} Noemí, si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha testificado contra mí y el Todopoderoso me ha hecho mal?».
es.B: Me fui llena, pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha traído de vuelta vacía. ¿Por qué me {{plural_you:llaman|llamáis}} Noemí? {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha dado testimonio contra mí, y el Todopoderoso me ha traído la desgracia».
es.R: Cuando me fui de aquí, mi vida estaba llena. Ahora {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha traído de vuelta sin nada. ¿Por qué me {{plural_you:llaman|llamáis}} Noemí? {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hablado en contra mía. El Dios Todopoderoso me ha traído desgracias».

fr.R: Quand je suis partie d’ici, ma vie était pleine. Maintenant, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a ramenée sans rien. Alors pourquoi m’appeler Noémi ? {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé contre moi. Dieu le Tout-Puissant m’a envoyé le malheur. »

vi.B: Tôi đã ra đi đầy đủ, nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đem tôi về tay trắng. Sao các chị còn gọi tôi là Na-ô-mi? {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã làm chứng nghịch lại tôi, và Đấng Toàn Năng đã giáng tai họa trên tôi."

decisions.choice: full ... empty: with a family, and without one
decisions.reason: Naomi left in a famine, so "full" is not wealth but her husband and two sons; "empty" is their loss. The Hebrew puts both words first for weight. Yet Ruth stands beside her as she speaks, and later Boaz will not send Ruth back to Naomi "empty" (3:17).

decisions.choice: has testified against me: has spoken as a witness against me
decisions.reason: With these vowels the verb means to answer or testify, and "against me" makes it a witness's word in a lawsuit (Exodus 20:16; Numbers 35:30). Naomi feels the LORD has spoken against her. The same letters can be read as "has afflicted me", as the ancient Greek translation does; the sense of hardship from God is the same.

decisions.choice: the Almighty has done harm to me
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring harm or trouble on someone. Naomi uses the two names of God side by side, the LORD and the Almighty (see verse 20), and holds him to account for her losses.

decisions.choice: has spoken against me
decisions.reason: Readable says in plain words what testifying against someone is.

decisions.choice: brought disaster (Balanced); brought trouble (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "done me harm"; Balanced and Readable use words for misfortune, since the verb here speaks of what happened to her, not of wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: the Almighty (Literal, Balanced); God All-Powerful (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

decisions.choice: Naomi calls the women of Bethlehem "các chị" and herself "tôi"
decisions.reason: Women of her own town whom she has known; "các chị" is warm but not familial, as their surprised question in verse 19 suggests.

en.L: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, with her, who returned from the fields of Moab. And they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
en.B: So Naomi came back, and with her came her daughter-in-law Ruth the Moabite, who had come back from the country of Moab. They arrived in Bethlehem as the barley harvest was beginning.
en.R: That is how Naomi came back from Moab, with Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, who came back with her. They reached Bethlehem just when people were starting to harvest the barley.

es.B: Así fue como Noemí regresó, y con ella regresó su nuera Rut la moabita, que había venido de la región de Moab. Llegaron a Belén cuando comenzaba la siega de la cebada.
es.R: Así fue como Noemí volvió de Moab, con Rut, su nuera moabita, que vino con ella. Llegaron a Belén justo cuando la gente comenzaba a cosechar la cebada.

vi.L: Vậy Na-ô-mi trở về, và Ru-tơ người Mô-áp, con dâu bà, cùng với bà, là người đã trở về từ đồng ruộng Mô-áp. Họ đến Bết-lê-hem vào đầu mùa gặt lúa mạch.

vi.R: Đó là cách Na-ô-mi trở về từ Mô-áp, cùng với Ru-tơ là con dâu người Mô-áp của bà. Họ đến Bết-lê-hem đúng lúc người ta bắt đầu gặt lúa mạch.

ko.L: 이렇게 나오미가 돌아왔고, 모압 들판에서 돌아온 그의 며느리 모압 여자 룻도 그와 함께 돌아왔다. 그들이 베들레헴에 이른 때는 보리를 거두기 시작할 무렵이었다.
ko.B: 이렇게 나오미는 돌아왔고, 모압 땅에서 함께 돌아온 그의 며느리 모압 여자 룻도 그와 함께 왔다. 그들이 베들레헴에 도착했을 때는 보리 추수가 시작될 무렵이었다.
ko.R: 이렇게 나오미는 모압에서 돌아왔다. 모압 여자인 며느리 룻도 그와 함께 돌아왔다. 그들이 베들레헴에 이른 때는 사람들이 막 보리를 거두기 시작할 무렵이었다.

pt.L: Assim voltou Noemi, e Rute, a moabita, a sua nora, com ela, a que voltou dos campos de Moabe. E elas chegaram a Belém no começo da colheita da cevada.
pt.B: Assim Noemi voltou, e com ela voltou também a nora, Rute, a moabita, que vinha de volta da terra de Moabe. Elas chegaram a Belém quando a colheita da cevada estava começando.
pt.R: Foi assim que Noemi voltou de Moabe com Rute, a sua nora moabita, que voltou com ela. Elas chegaram a Belém bem quando o povo estava começando a colher a cevada.

decisions.choice: who returned: said of Ruth
decisions.reason: The words most likely describe Ruth, the Moabite who "returned" from Moab though she had never lived in Judah, as she is described again in 2:6. The chapter's key word now includes her: Naomi's return is hers too.

decisions.choice: the beginning of the barley harvest: spring, the first grain harvest
decisions.reason: Barley ripened first, in spring about the time of Passover (Leviticus 23:10-11), before the wheat. The famine is over, the fields of Bethlehem are full, and the scene is set for chapter 2, where Ruth gleans in the harvest.

decisions.choice: returned ... at the beginning of harvest: the empty return meets a full land
decisions.reason: Naomi says she has come back empty (verse 21), but the chapter ends with Ruth at her side and the harvest beginning, the LORD's gift of food (verse 6). The story will move from emptiness to fullness.

decisions.choice: came back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "came back" for both uses of "return", keeping the repeated word; Literal keeps "returned".

decisions.choice: voltar, every time
decisions.reason: The chapter's key word (m3 of verse 6) is "voltar" at every level, from verse 6 to here, also for Ruth, who "returns" to a land she has never seen (m1); Readable says "ir com" only in verse 10, as the English does. Varying it with "regressar" would hide the repetition.
